Image: wheel zooms, middle drag pans, double-click fits; the crop tool returns a rectangle, and Escape restores the previous selection. Gradient: double-click adds an interpolated stop, drag moves it, right-click removes a stop when more than two remain. Host color editors change stop colors. Texture lifetime, color management and document transforms remain host-owned.

The transform gizmo's handles are ImGui items: over a canvas (imageViewport, viewport, CanvasScope) they take the hover and the click, so nothing underneath reacts. Host items drawn over a canvas get the same by calling markCanvasOverlay() each frame. Viewport: Alt-left drag orbits, middle drag pans, wheel changes distance. Host renderers produce the texture; CyUI does not render a 3D scene. Transform2D rotation is radians. Ctrl snaps rotation to 15-degree increments. Gizmo3DOptions selects ImGuizmo operation/mode, snap, orthographic view, revision and enabled state. Link CyUI::ImGuizmo only when a compatible host target is supplied.

Commands, logs and documents#

  • rankCommands(commands, query) matches every search word and returns stable ranked indices. commandPalette(id, open, state, commands, size) displays a modal palette with keyboard navigation and returns a requested command ID. Disabled entries do not execute; the host maps IDs to actions.
  • LogBuffer(capacity,maxBytes) provides synchronized append/clear/snapshot. logView(id, LogState&, buffer, size) filters/follows bounded cached rows and returns a selected ID; LogState.levels masks debug/info/warning/error. diagnosticList(id, rows, size) displays source/line/column/message and returns a requested diagnostic ID. The host resolves source navigation.
  • Document::setMarkdown caches CommonMark/GFM blocks, nested inline styles, tasks, sized native images, spoilers, tables, anchors and code. documentView returns link/media/task/resize requests and selectable visible text. Assign nonblocking DocumentServices for cached native images and link previews.
  • transcript uses the same renderer and stable message IDs for streamed content.
  • Optional DocumentEditor provides Live/Source/Split/Reading modes, native block rich input, shared C++ Undo, toolbars, search, clipboard/drop hooks and spelling.
  • Optional DocumentIO reads/writes .md/.cymd buffers (UTF-8/UTF-16/BOM, stored/DEFLATE ZIP, resource budgets) and converts clipboard HTML.
  • Optional mediaPlayer draws native controls around an existing MediaBackend.
  • Optional DocumentWebAdapter connects activated embeds to an existing WebBackend, from CyUI Web/CEF or the host. The host still pumps its runtime.

See the native Markdown guide for contracts, recipes and limits. Unknown HTML stays text. No renderer runs scripts, opens links or fetches URLs. Gallery: 18 reader/chat, 24 editor, 25 simulated host playback.

Optional Web / CEF#

webPanel, WebBackend/WebPlacement/WebInput, WebPolicy/webOrigin, webThemeJson and webEventJson form the engine-independent browser module. createWebCEF, webCEFApp and webCEFBrowser provide the optional CEF implementation. The browser draws in a host-owned texture and shares CyUI theme roles through CSS. See WEB.md for the complete lifecycle, native/Python recipes, TypeScript bridge, CyMD iframe protocol, origin checks, process sandbox and OS packaging. CEF is separate from Core and from the module's neutral API. The local validated runtime is Windows; Linux/macOS build/deployment validation is explicitly pending.

Rules when using it:

  • Pump CefDoMessageLoopWork() (Python runtime.pump()) outside the ImGui frame, before NewFrame. WebCEFOptions::upload and the optional release callback run inside it; release(texture) comes once after the browser closed: free that texture only after the frames that used it (Python: create(..., release=)).
  • external events are page requests, never commands. Only WebPolicy::externalSchemes (default http/https) are reported; check userGesture, mainFrame and sourceOrigin, apply your own allow-list and ask the user before opening anything with the shell. Sub-frame popups without a gesture are dropped.
  • WebEventKind::dropped (data = count) reports events discarded by the queue caps (maxQueuedEvents, maxQueuedErrors for errors/console) or by policy.
  • WebPanelOptions::focus is one-shot (taken on a false -> true change). A focused panel owns the keys it forwards, so ImGui nav and other widgets do not act on them.
  • Backend calls must run on the CEF UI thread; others are ignored. The supplied bridge, helper and demo run CEF unsandboxed on Windows (WEB.md "Process sandbox").

RampStyle offers themed, intensity, frequency and monochrome ramps; all built-in colors come from the active semantic palette. Intensity goes from a quiet background toward hot levels; frequency grading progresses from low to high frequencies. ColorRamp.colors optionally borrows 1..64 evenly spaced palette colors. Invalid counts fall back to the selected built-in ramp. sampleRamp clamps fractions and interpolates; missing fractions select its low end. drawColorScale(rect, ramp, range, unit, vertical, logarithmic) draws inside the current canvas clip without reserving an item. A vertical scale has its minimum at the bottom; logarithmic=true positions its frequency ticks logarithmically. Scrolling spectrograms. timeHorizontal is the default; timeVertical places frequency horizontally. reverseTime reverses only the time direction. State axes remain semantic X=time, Y=frequency in every orientation, and mouse results remain time/Hz. colorByFrequency=true uses frequency for hue and intensity for opacity; its legend then shows Hz. SpectrogramResult.bounds excludes the optional color legend, so legend pixels cannot select a data cell. legend defaults to false for existing layouts, and hides itself when the widget is too narrow to keep the data readable. cpp Copy cyui :: SpectrogramHistory history ; // persist; reset once when the stream format changes history . reset ( 256 , 128 , 0.01 , { 20 , 20000 } , true ) ; // capacity, bins, hop seconds, Hz, log bins // Once per new analysis frame, outside draw: history.append(preparedBins); cyui :: SpectrogramState state ; // persist per panel state . window = 2.0 ; cyui :: SpectrogramOptions options ; options . orientation = cyui :: SpectrogramOrientation :: timeVertical ; options . reverseTime = true ; options . legend = true ; options . ramp . style = cyui :: RampStyle :: intensity ; cyui :: spectrogram ( "##history" , state , history . view ( ) , cyui :: dp ( 0 , 240 ) , options ) ; History validates its format, keeps chronological order through wraparound, and accepts only a complete column with the configured bin count. The fixed hop defines cell coverage from the configured start time; append NaN columns for missing frames. Invalid resets/appends preserve the preceding state. Capacity × bins is capped at 4,194,304 float cells (up to 32 MiB for ring plus ordered snapshot). view() caches a borrowed ordered snapshot until data changes. Synchronize producer/UI access in the host. clear(start) starts a new time origin. The state overload follows the latest window seconds; zoom/pan pauses following, double-click resumes it, or set followLatest=true explicitly. The original PlotState overload remains manual. Persistence and spatial views. Supply stereoDensity with prepared L/R points and a revision that changes only with new input. Its default M/S projection is S=(L-R)/2 and M=(L+R)/2; midSide=false displays L/R directly. It reserves a square. spatialScope takes SpatialSample{frequencyHz, normalizedPan, levelDb} with pan in [-1,+1]. Its view is pan × frequency, logarithmic in frequency by default. SpatialScopeOptions.levels normalizes level intensity; colorFrequency sets the frequency grading domain, independently of zoom. colorByFrequency=false selects intensity grading instead. Invalid/nonfinite samples are skipped. Each state owns a DensityState with clear() . Repeated input revisions decay without reinjection; new revisions add energy. PersistenceOptions controls resolution (96 by default, clamped to 16..256), halfLife (0.5 seconds), exposure, pointRadius (design pixels), diffusion (per second), axes/navigation, ramp and maxPoints (65,536). A nonpositive half-life shows only the current frame. View, projection and resolution changes clear incompatible history. Oversized input is reported as series 1 in skippedSeries . Use one state per panel/ImGui context. Dense plots require the renderer's normal ImGui VtxOffset support; reduce point, cell or density budgets for renderers with a smaller index budget. Python mirrors these models with snake_case fields. Use ColorRamp('intensity') , spectrogram(..., orientation='time_vertical', reverse_time=True, legend=True) , band_spectrum(..., floor=-90) , stereo_density(..., revision, persistence=options) and spatial_scope(..., revision, persistence=options) . PersistenceOptions is a dataclass. draw_color_scale(top, bottom, ramp, values, unit='', vertical=True, logarithmic=False) uses screen coordinates within the current clip. Code, editing and Git-style diff presentation # CodeDocument::setText(text, language, revision) preserves original UTF-8 bytes, tabs, CRLF and final-newline state. Display lines expand tabs to four columns and carry lexical spans. Languages include plain, C++, C#, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, GLSL, HLSL, JSON, Lua, SQL, INI and Markdown. Lexical coloring is a presentation heuristic; supply semantic parser/LSP results as overlays when needed. setOverlays(SourceSpan[], revision) accepts zero-based lines and raw UTF-8 byte offsets. Stale revisions and offsets inside a code point are rejected. tokenColor(role, background) maps token roles through the current palette, adjusting toward the text role for contrast. paintCodeLine draws prepared spans. codeViewer(id, CodeViewState&, document, size, annotations) provides line numbers, search/next, selected/focused line, annotation hover and navigation IDs. CodeEditor::setText/text/setLanguage/setReadOnly/draw wraps the optional MIT native TextEditor. draw returns document-changed. native() exposes advanced TextEditor hooks for completion, annotations, cursors, wrapping and Undo/Redo; include TextEditor.h and handle document storage/revisions in the host. DiffDocument::setTexts(before, after, language, workBudget) prepares a bounded comparison; setUnified(text, language) reads a unified patch. rows , pairs , hunks , columns , revision , approximate expose prepared presentation data. diffViewer(id, DiffState&, document, size) offers unified/side-by-side modes, one shared vertical canvas for both columns, a shared horizontal text offset with fixed line-number gutters, hunk/search navigation, inline changed ranges and old/new line navigation results. Final-newline-only changes are represented; CRLF and LF lines compare equal, with a notice row when line endings differ. DiffState::scroll reports the current vertical offset; assigning it requests a scroll. Hosts should call this viewer directly, without mirroring child-window offsets. See DIFF.md for details and native regression coverage. expandTabs(text, tabSize) widens tabs to the next stop as displayed; displayOffset(raw, byteOffset, tabSize) maps a raw byte offset to that display text. cpp Copy cyui :: DiffDocument comparison ; comparison . setTexts ( beforeText , afterText , cyui :: CodeLanguage :: cpp ) ; cyui :: DiffState view ; auto clicked = cyui :: diffViewer ( "##comparison" , view , comparison , cyui :: dp ( 0 , 400 ) ) ; if ( clicked . newLine > 0 ) host . openNewDocumentAt ( clicked . newLine ) ; Do not call setTexts on unchanged large documents every frame. Code and Diff do not depend on Git, LSP, a compiler or CodeEditor. Host repository/authentication, review comments, merge resolution and actions stay outside the renderer. Inspector and assets # Property supports bool, int64, double, strings, choices, readOnly/password/ multiline flags and optional bounds. Set integerMinimum/integerMaximum for exact integer bounds; do not convert int64 through double. inspector(id, state, properties, revision, validator) returns PropertyEdit entries. The validator returns an error string; invalid drafts remain visible without committing. assetBrowser(id, AssetState&, items, size) uses AssetItem{id,parent,label,type, thumbnail,folder,favorite}. State owns query, folder, selected IDs and grid/list mode. It returns open/favorite/rename/remove requests. It performs no filesystem operation. CYUI_ASSET carries the stable numeric ID for host drag/drop handling. Folder parents and thumbnails are host data; querying/scanning/loading stays outside. Images, viewport and optional 3D gizmo # API Use imageViewport(id, ImageState&, ImageData, size, ImageTool) Texture/UV crop, checkerboard, fit/zoom/pan, pixel hover and crop edit proposal sampleGradient(stops, position, linearLight) Sample unordered stops using sRGB or explicit linear-light interpolation gradientEditor(id, GradientState&, stops, size, linearLight, revision) Select/drag/add/remove stops; returns edits cameraPosition/cameraViewMatrix(OrbitCamera) Arbitrary up axis, column-major right-handed camera viewport(id, ViewportState&, ImageData, size, navigation) Aspect-preserving scene texture, UV picking, camera interaction transformGizmo(id, TransformState&, Transform2D, options) 2D move/scale/rotation overlay, projection/unprojection callbacks gizmo3D(id, Gizmo3DState&, matrix, view, projection, rect, options) Optional host ImGuizmo adapter for column-major scene transforms Image: wheel zooms, middle drag pans, double-click fits; the crop tool returns a rectangle, and Escape restores the previous selection. Gradient: double-click adds an interpolated stop, drag moves it, right-click removes a stop when more than two remain. Host color editors change stop colors. Texture lifetime, color management and document transforms remain host-owned. The transform gizmo's handles are ImGui items: over a canvas (imageViewport, viewport, CanvasScope) they take the hover and the click, so nothing underneath reacts. Host items drawn over a canvas get the same by calling markCanvasOverlay() each frame. Viewport: Alt-left drag orbits, middle drag pans, wheel changes distance. Host renderers produce the texture; CyUI does not render a 3D scene. Transform2D rotation is radians. Ctrl snaps rotation to 15-degree increments. Gizmo3DOptions selects ImGuizmo operation/mode, snap, orthographic view, revision and enabled state. Link CyUI::ImGuizmo only when a compatible host target is supplied. Commands, logs and documents # rankCommands(commands, query) matches every search word and returns stable ranked indices. commandPalette(id, open, state, commands, size) displays a modal palette with keyboard navigation and returns a requested command ID. Disabled entries do not execute; the host maps IDs to actions. LogBuffer(capacity,maxBytes) provides synchronized append/clear/snapshot. logView(id, LogState&, buffer, size) filters/follows bounded cached rows and returns a selected ID; LogState.levels masks debug/info/warning/error. diagnosticList(id, rows, size) displays source/line/column/message and returns a requested diagnostic ID. The host resolves source navigation. Document::setMarkdown caches CommonMark/GFM blocks, nested inline styles, tasks, sized native images, spoilers, tables, anchors and code. documentView returns link/media/task/resize requests and selectable visible text. Assign nonblocking DocumentServices for cached native images and link previews. transcript uses the same renderer and stable message IDs for streamed content. Optional DocumentEditor provides Live/Source/Split/Reading modes, native block rich input, shared C++ Undo, toolbars, search, clipboard/drop hooks and spelling. Optional DocumentIO reads/writes .md / .cymd buffers (UTF-8/UTF-16/BOM, stored/DEFLATE ZIP, resource budgets) and converts clipboard HTML. Optional mediaPlayer draws native controls around an existing MediaBackend . Optional DocumentWebAdapter connects activated embeds to an existing WebBackend , from CyUI Web/CEF or the host. The host still pumps its runtime. See the native Markdown guide for contracts, recipes and limits. Unknown HTML stays text. No renderer runs scripts, opens links or fetches URLs. Gallery: 18 reader/chat, 24 editor, 25 simulated host playback. Optional Web / CEF # webPanel , WebBackend/WebPlacement/WebInput, WebPolicy/webOrigin, webThemeJson and webEventJson form the engine-independent browser module. createWebCEF , webCEFApp and webCEFBrowser provide the optional CEF implementation. The browser draws in a host-owned texture and shares CyUI theme roles through CSS. See WEB.md for the complete lifecycle, native/Python recipes, TypeScript bridge, CyMD iframe protocol, origin checks, process sandbox and OS packaging. CEF is separate from Core and from the module's neutral API. The local validated runtime is Windows; Linux/macOS build/deployment validation is explicitly pending. Rules when using it: Pump CefDoMessageLoopWork() (Python runtime.pump() ) outside the ImGui frame, before NewFrame . WebCEFOptions::upload and the optional release callback run inside it; release(texture) comes once after the browser closed: free that texture only after the frames that used it (Python: create(..., release=) ). external events are page requests, never commands. Only WebPolicy::externalSchemes (default http/https) are reported; check userGesture , mainFrame and sourceOrigin , apply your own allow-list and ask the user before opening anything with the shell. Sub-frame popups without a gesture are dropped. WebEventKind::dropped (data = count) reports events discarded by the queue caps ( maxQueuedEvents , maxQueuedErrors for errors/console) or by policy. WebPanelOptions::focus is one-shot (taken on a false -> true change). A focused panel owns the keys it forwards, so ImGui nav and other widgets do not act on them. Backend calls must run on the CEF UI thread; others are ignored. The supplied bridge, helper and demo run CEF unsandboxed on Windows (WEB.md "Process sandbox"). Python examples # python Copy from cyui_modules . curves import CurvePoint , CurveState , curve_editor from cyui_modules . common import Range state = CurveState ( ) state . view . x . view = Range ( 0 , 10 ) state . view . y . view = Range ( 0 , 1 ) points = [ CurvePoint ( 1 , 0 , .2 ) , CurvePoint ( 2 , 10 , .8 ) ] # Each ImGui frame: edit = curve_editor ( 'automation' , state , points , ( 0 , 260 ) , revision = revision ) if edit . committed : points = edit . value Python optional APIs are snake_case equivalents in the packages listed in MODULES.md . Python source offsets for SourceSpan are raw UTF-8 bytes; displayed lexer spans use Python character indices. Do not mix those two coordinate systems. CodeEditor in Python offers native ImGui multiline Undo plus a syntax preview; C++ TextEditor advanced callbacks are not exposed there. CEFRuntime is an explicit optional browser loader; importing model modules is independent of imgui-bundle, NumPy, audio/video or browser engines. cyui::CurveState state; // persist with the panel std::vector<cyui::CurvePoint> points; // sorted, finite, stable nonzero IDs cyui::CurveOptions options; options.revision = document.revision; options.snap = 0.25; auto edit = cyui::curveEditor("##automation", state, points, cyui::dp(0, 260), options); if (edit.committed()) document.commitCurve(edit.value); cyui::PlotState state{{{20, 20000}, true}, {{-90, 0}, false}}; cyui::PlotSeries line{1, "Spectrum", preparedPoints, cyui::PlotStyle::line, 1}; cyui::PlotOptions options; options.formatX = [](double hz) { return formatFrequency(hz); }; auto hover = cyui::plot("##response", state, {&line, 1}, cyui::dp(0, 220), options); std::vector<cyui::Point> samples{{0, 0}, {.02, 1}, {.3, .4}, {.7, .4}, {1, 0}}; const cyui::EnvelopeStage phases[]{ {{0, .02}, "A"}, {{.02, .3}, "D"}, {{.3, .7}, "S"}, {{.7, 1}, "R"}}; cyui::EnvelopeData data{samples, {phases, 4}}; data.playhead = .5; data.level = .4; // optional live host measurements cyui::EnvelopeOptions options; options.time = {0, 1}; options.levels = {0, 1}; options.timePower = .6; const auto hit = cyui::envelope("##env", data, cyui::dp(0, 180), options); // hit.mouse is time/level, even with a nonlinear time display. // Keep this state with the instrument UI. Samples and handle positions come from the host. const cyui::Point phaseWidths[]{{0, 0}, {.02, .20}, {.3, .50}, {.7, .75}, {1, 1}}; data.timeKnots = {phaseWidths, 5}; cyui::EnvelopeEditState& gesture = instrumentUi.decayGesture; const cyui::EnvelopeHandle decay{1, {.3, .4}, cyui::EnvelopeAxes::both}; const auto result = cyui::envelope("##env", gesture, data, {&decay, 1}, cyui::dp(0, 100), options); if (result.edit.committed()) { const auto p = result.edit.value.position; instrument.setDecayAndSustain(p.x - attackEndTime, p.y); // one host undo transaction } cyui::ResponseState state; // persist per panel std::vector<cyui::ResponsePoint> bands{{1, 120, 4}, {2, 1800, -7}}; cyui::ResponseOptions options; options.revision = revision; auto result = cyui::filterResponse("##eq", state, gainCurves, phaseCurves, bands, cyui::dp(0, 240), options); if (result.points.committed()) commitBands(result.points.value); // one Undo entry // During a drag, evaluate preview curves from state.preview. cyui::SpectrogramHistory history; // persist; reset once when the stream format changes history.reset(256, 128, 0.01, {20, 20000}, true); // capacity, bins, hop seconds, Hz, log bins // Once per new analysis frame, outside draw: history.append(preparedBins); cyui::SpectrogramState state; // persist per panel state.window = 2.0; cyui::SpectrogramOptions options; options.orientation = cyui::SpectrogramOrientation::timeVertical; options.reverseTime = true; options.legend = true; options.ramp.style = cyui::RampStyle::intensity; cyui::spectrogram("##history", state, history.view(), cyui::dp(0, 240), options); cyui::DiffDocument comparison; comparison.setTexts(beforeText, afterText, cyui::CodeLanguage::cpp); cyui::DiffState view; auto clicked = cyui::diffViewer("##comparison", view, comparison, cyui::dp(0, 400)); if (clicked.newLine > 0) host.openNewDocumentAt(clicked.newLine); from cyui_modules.curves import CurvePoint, CurveState, curve_editor from cyui_modules.common import Range state = CurveState() state.view.x.view = Range(0, 10) state.view.y.view = Range(0, 1) points = [CurvePoint(1, 0, .2), CurvePoint(2, 10, .8)] # Each ImGui frame: edit = curve_editor('automation', state, points, (0, 260), revision=revision) if edit.committed: points = edit.value

pages.description: Select optional modules for CyUI integrators.
pages.html:
CyUI 1.2 provides a common Dear ImGui foundation and independently selectable interface modules. All CyUI code is MIT licensed. Applications own their models, engines, files, services, validation and Undo history.

Localization in every integration#

Core includes English (default), French and extensible translation catalogs. Use stable translated labels when migrating application interfaces. C++, Python, Web and Unreal usage, font requirements and host responsibilities are described in LOCALIZATION.md.

Targets and dependencies#

CyUI::Core contains themes, localization, quick filters, fonts, icons, ordinary widgets, layout and notifications. Modules link Core automatically. The following targets are implemented:

Menu/panel filtering is opt-in through Core's TextFilter, filterBox, filterMenu and the filtered panel header. Inspector accepts an optional filter without adding a dependency. See FILTERING.md.

CMake target Public header Interface Additional CyUI dependency
CyUI::Audio modules/Audio.h Knobs, faders, peak/RMS meters Core
CyUI::Canvas modules/Canvas.h Double coordinates, grid, clipping, pan/zoom Core
CyUI::Plots modules/Plots.h Linear/log axes, reusable curve fills, lines, steps, points, bars, histograms, heatmaps Canvas
CyUI::Curves modules/Curves.h Keyframes, Bezier handles, selection, snap, copy/paste Plots
CyUI::Nodes modules/Nodes.h Cards, pins, links, layout, move/connect/remove requests Canvas
CyUI::Timeline modules/Timeline.h Lanes, clips, markers, ruler, move/trim, range selection Canvas
CyUI::AudioViews modules/AudioViews.h ADSR/AHDSR envelope displays, waveforms, filled/band spectra, scrolling spectrograms, spatial/persistent scopes, meters, EQ and dynamics Plots
CyUI::Code modules/Code.h Paged line contracts/builders, source viewer, 102 syntax modes, extensible registry, semantic overlays, annotations, search Core + selected Lexilla engines + system threads
CyUI::Diff modules/Diff.h Unified/split diff, line numbers, hunk navigation, inline ranges Code
CyUI::CodeEditor modules/CodeEditor.h In-memory TextEditor and host-backed PagedCodeEditor (distinct capabilities) Code + MIT TextEditor, C++20
CyUI::Inspector modules/Inspector.h Typed properties, exact int64, validation, draft edits Core
CyUI::Assets modules/Assets.h Hierarchical folder navigation, grid/list, search, thumbnails, drag/drop Core
CyUI::Images modules/Images.h Texture viewport, checkerboard, crop, gradient stops Canvas
CyUI::Viewport modules/Viewport.h Host-rendered scene surface, orbit camera, 2D transform overlay Images
CyUI::Commands modules/Commands.h Searchable keyboard command palette Core
CyUI::Diagnostics modules/Diagnostics.h Bounded thread-safe logs, filters, diagnostic navigation Core + system threads
CyUI::DocumentViews modules/DocumentViews.h Native Markdown/GFM, images, tasks, spoilers, tables and transcripts Code, Images, MIT MD4C
CyUI::DocumentEditor modules/DocumentEditor.h Live/source/split/reading editor DocumentViews, CodeEditor, DataGrid
CyUI::DocumentIO modules/DocumentIO.h Markdown/CyMD buffers, HTML clipboard DocumentViews, miniz
CyUI::DocumentWeb modules/DocumentWeb.h Optional existing web backend adapter DocumentViews, Web
CyUI::Media modules/Media.h Native playback controls with a host engine Images
CyUI::Web modules/Web.h Browser panel, texture/input contract, origin policy, messages, theme bridge Core
CyUI::DataGrid modules/DataGrid.h Editable cells, rectangular ranges, clipboard, row/column structure, formats and undo Core
CyUI::Spreadsheet modules/Spreadsheet.h Worksheets, formula bar, bounded calculation and workbook undo DataGrid
CyUI::RichDocument modules/RichDocument.h Paginated document editor, rich paragraphs, tables, images and page settings DocumentEditor, DataGrid
CyUI::OfficeIO modules/OfficeIO.h ODT/ODS, DOCX/XLSX and flat ODF imports/exports with issues RichDocument, Spreadsheet, DocumentIO, MIT pugixml

| CyUI::Hierarchy | modules/Hierarchy.h | Scene/layer tree, selection, reparent, rename, visibility/locking | Core | | CyUI::DataView | modules/DataView.h | Virtual tables, all Inspector editors, atomic typed TSV paste | Inspector (Core transitively) | | CyUI::FilePicker | modules/FilePicker.h | Host/VFS open/save/directory selection, filters and overwrite confirmation | Core | | CyUI::Gallery | Gallery.h | Examples and theme editor | Enabled modules only |

Header paths are relative to include/cyui/. CyUI::Code::Diff is an alias for CyUI::Diff. CyUI::CyUI is the compatibility umbrella linking all modules selected in this build. A module is a static library, not a dynamically loaded plugin.

Optional external adapters:

Target Enablement Dependency
CyUI::ImGuizmo Set CYUI_IMGUIZMO_TARGET to an existing host target; select Viewport Host's MIT ImGuizmo; adapters/ImGuizmo.h
CyUI::WebCEF CYUI_BUILD_WEB_CEF=ON; select Web Host CEF SDK/runtime; adapters/WebCEF.h, C++20

Neither adapter is downloaded or enabled by CYUI_MODULES=All. The Web module is usable with a host backend; the supplied browser implementation is CEF. See WEB.md for platform support, process lifecycle and deployment. WebCEF hands the host a texture release callback, reports external requests with userGesture/mainFrame/sourceOrigin (schemes limited by WebPolicy::externalSchemes) and counts discarded events in dropped events. The supplied bridge and helper run CEF unsandboxed on Windows (see WEB.md).

The optional Unreal Editor module packages selected CyUI modules for embedding in an existing plugin's Source/CyUI folder or sharing through one provider plugin. It provides a Slate renderer/input backend without menus or demo windows. Prepare it separately with tools/package_unreal.py --layout module (default); it is not a CMake target or a dependency of Core. A redistributed plugin embeds it under a unique name with --module-name, or depends on the shared provider.

Select only what an application needs#

cmake
set(CYUI_IMGUI_TARGET app_imgui)set(CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_AUDIO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_GALLERY OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_MODULES "Code;Diff;Inspector" CACHE STRING "" FORCE)add_subdirectory(external/CyUI)target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE CyUI::Diff CyUI::Inspector)
cpp
#include <cyui/Core.h>#include <cyui/modules/Diff.h>#include <cyui/modules/Inspector.h>

Dependencies are selected automatically: Diff enables Code; it does not enable CodeEditor, audio, plots or a browser. Link explicit targets to keep public feature macros and dependencies restricted to the consumer. CYUI_HAS_CODE, CYUI_HAS_DIFF, etc. are public definitions of their respective targets.

CYUI_MODULES accepts a semicolon list, Core, an empty list, or All. The standalone full demo defaults to All. Embedded builds and standalone builds with the demo disabled default to no new optional modules. Audio and Gallery retain their original ON defaults; disable those explicitly when not used. CyUI::Core never links them. The old Widgets.h/CyUI.h declarations remain source compatible.

Without CMake, compile the five Core sources and only the selected src/modules/<Name>.cpp files plus their dependency closure. Define the matching CYUI_HAS_<NAME> macros for Gallery/CyUI.h. CodeEditor also needs src/modules/PagedCodeEditor.cpp, TextEditor.cpp, its include directory and C++20. Code and its dependents additionally compile src/modules/code/*.cpp, the bundled third_party/lexilla/lexlib/*.cxx and lexers/*.cxx, with Lexilla include/lexlib and Scintilla include directories. Define CYUI_CODE_LANGUAGE_CATALOGUE=1 for the extended C++ catalogue API. build_demo.bat is the complete Windows demo build.

Shared data and edit contract#

  • Give every object a stable, nonzero uint64 ID: results that return a bare ID (command palette, log/diagnostic rows, plot series, annotations) use 0 for none. Gestures track their targets with flags, so a 0 ID still drags and selects. Keep one state object per view.
  • Wheel zoom and pan keep ranges usable: a step that would overflow a log axis or shrink a span below what its magnitude resolves (|value| x 1e-12) is ignored. Selection ranges are reported ordered (min <= max).
  • ArrayView and callbacks borrow data for the call; keep it alive while drawing.
  • Curve points are finite and sorted by time; timeline durations are positive. Units, snapping policy, graph types and interpolation belong to the host.
  • Editors return Edit<T> proposals with begin, update, commit, cancel. Atomic actions may return commit directly. Preview state never mutates the host. Validate and apply a committed proposal as one Undo transaction. Increment the supplied revision when replacing host data during a gesture to cancel stale edits.
  • Ordinary rendering and model preparation run on the host UI thread. LogBuffer append/clear/snapshot are synchronized and may be called from producer threads.
  • Colors use palette roles; UI geometry uses dp/style. Gradient colors, plot values, textures and scene matrices are application data.
  • No module reads projects, executes Git actions, starts a terminal process, decodes audio/video, computes FFTs or runs a language server. Clipboard actions are local UI requests. Web explicitly creates a browser only when selected.

Prepare documents/envelopes when data changes. Draw visible rows using cached models, and supply visible/bounded datasets for graphs and timelines. Plots accept at most 65,536 points per series by default and report oversized IDs in skippedSeries; call reducePlot or query a host index before drawing. Heatmaps bound the displayed cells to 256 per axis. Diff uses patience anchors and bounded LCS (4 million cells by default), exposing approximate() when an unmatched region is displayed as a full replacement. Both source sides are retained; CRLF and LF lines compare equal and a notice row reports differing line endings. Source/Markdown inputs are limited to 32 MiB; large files need host paging. Logs default to 10,000 rows / 8 MiB. Waveforms consume prepared min/max envelopes.

Python#

sh
python -m pip install -e ".[ui]"

cyui remains the existing theme/widget API. cyui_modules contains optional audio, canvas, plots, curves, nodes, timeline, audioviews, code, diff, inspector, assets, images, viewport, commands, diagnostics, documents (documentviews alias), web and cef. Import models without loading imgui-bundle; drawing imports it lazily. No NumPy, media decoder or 3D engine is required.

Python uses the same IDs, ranges, palette roles, edit phases, origin policy and bounded diff algorithm. Its CodeEditor uses ImGui multiline editing with native Undo and a live syntax preview. The richer C++ TextEditor backend has its own API; Python does not pretend to expose its multiple cursors/completion hooks. cyui_modules.cef.CEFRuntime loads the optional C ABI library/helper explicitly; CEF binaries are not included in the Python package. See WEB.md.

Paged documents#

CodePaging.h belongs to Code (C++17); PagedCodeEditor.h belongs to CodeEditor (C++20). The provider guide specifies bounded reads, UTF-16 positions, contextual syntax and host-owned transactions. The paged editor does not inherit the classic lexer's 32 MiB snapshot limit or copy the whole file. Per-page and input budgets still apply. This native C++ API has no Python or Web binding yet. Source packaging includes it when CodeEditor is selected; Unreal Editor compilation and platform input still require host validation.

Native Markdown guide.

Editor tools#

Typed Inspector JSON, expressions, hierarchies, tables, file picker, commands and graph/timeline editing.

scene surface, orbit camera, 2D transform overlay Images CyUI::Commands modules/Commands.h Searchable keyboard command palette Core CyUI::Diagnostics modules/Diagnostics.h Bounded thread-safe logs, filters, diagnostic navigation Core + system threads CyUI::DocumentViews modules/DocumentViews.h Native Markdown/GFM, images, tasks, spoilers, tables and transcripts Code, Images, MIT MD4C DocumentViews, miniz CyUI::DocumentWeb modules/DocumentWeb.h Optional existing web backend adapter DocumentViews, Web CyUI::Media modules/Media.h Native playback controls with a host engine Images CyUI::Web modules/Web.h Browser panel, texture/input contract, origin policy, messages, theme bridge Core CyUI::DataGrid modules/DataGrid.h Editable cells, rectangular ranges, clipboard, row/column structure, formats and undo Core CyUI::Spreadsheet modules/Spreadsheet.h Worksheets, formula bar, bounded calculation and workbook undo DataGrid CyUI::RichDocument modules/RichDocument.h Paginated document editor, rich paragraphs, tables, images and page settings DocumentEditor, DataGrid CyUI::OfficeIO modules/OfficeIO.h ODT/ODS, DOCX/XLSX and flat ODF imports/exports with issues RichDocument, Spreadsheet, DocumentIO, MIT pugixml | CyUI::Hierarchy | modules/Hierarchy.h | Scene/layer tree, selection, reparent, rename, visibility/locking | Core | | CyUI::DataView | modules/DataView.h | Virtual tables, all Inspector editors, atomic typed TSV paste | Inspector (Core transitively) | | CyUI::FilePicker | modules/FilePicker.h | Host/VFS open/save/directory selection, filters and overwrite confirmation | Core | | CyUI::Gallery | Gallery.h | Examples and theme editor | Enabled modules only | Header paths are relative to include/cyui/ . CyUI::Code::Diff is an alias for CyUI::Diff . CyUI::CyUI is the compatibility umbrella linking all modules selected in this build. A module is a static library, not a dynamically loaded plugin. Optional external adapters: Target Enablement Dependency CyUI::ImGuizmo Set CYUI_IMGUIZMO_TARGET to an existing host target; select Viewport Host's MIT ImGuizmo; adapters/ImGuizmo.h CyUI::WebCEF CYUI_BUILD_WEB_CEF=ON ; select Web Host CEF SDK/runtime; adapters/WebCEF.h , C++20 Neither adapter is downloaded or enabled by CYUI_MODULES=All . The Web module is usable with a host backend; the supplied browser implementation is CEF. See WEB.md for platform support, process lifecycle and deployment. WebCEF hands the host a texture release callback, reports external requests with userGesture / mainFrame / sourceOrigin (schemes limited by WebPolicy::externalSchemes ) and counts discarded events in dropped events. The supplied bridge and helper run CEF unsandboxed on Windows (see WEB.md). The optional Unreal Editor module packages selected CyUI modules for embedding in an existing plugin's Source/CyUI folder or sharing through one provider plugin. It provides a Slate renderer/input backend without menus or demo windows. Prepare it separately with tools/package_unreal.py --layout module (default); it is not a CMake target or a dependency of Core. A redistributed plugin embeds it under a unique name with --module-name , or depends on the shared provider. Select only what an application needs # cmake Copy set ( CYUI_IMGUI_TARGET app_imgui ) set ( CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE ) set ( CYUI_BUILD_AUDIO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE ) set ( CYUI_BUILD_GALLERY OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE ) set ( CYUI_MODULES "Code;Diff;Inspector" CACHE STRING "" FORCE ) add_subdirectory ( external/CyUI ) target_link_libraries ( app PRIVATE CyUI::Diff CyUI::Inspector ) cpp Copy # include <cyui/Core.h> # include <cyui/modules/Diff.h> # include <cyui/modules/Inspector.h> Dependencies are selected automatically: Diff enables Code; it does not enable CodeEditor, audio, plots or a browser. Link explicit targets to keep public feature macros and dependencies restricted to the consumer. CYUI_HAS_CODE , CYUI_HAS_DIFF , etc. are public definitions of their respective targets. CYUI_MODULES accepts a semicolon list, Core , an empty list, or All . The standalone full demo defaults to All. Embedded builds and standalone builds with the demo disabled default to no new optional modules. Audio and Gallery retain their original ON defaults; disable those explicitly when not used. CyUI::Core never links them. The old Widgets.h/CyUI.h declarations remain source compatible. Without CMake, compile the five Core sources and only the selected src/modules/<Name>.cpp files plus their dependency closure. Define the matching CYUI_HAS_<NAME> macros for Gallery/CyUI.h. CodeEditor also needs src/modules/PagedCodeEditor.cpp , TextEditor.cpp, its include directory and C++20. Code and its dependents additionally compile src/modules/code/*.cpp , the bundled third_party/lexilla/lexlib/*.cxx and lexers/*.cxx , with Lexilla include/lexlib and Scintilla include directories. Define CYUI_CODE_LANGUAGE_CATALOGUE=1 for the extended C++ catalogue API. build_demo.bat is the complete Windows demo build. Shared data and edit contract # Give every object a stable, nonzero uint64 ID: results that return a bare ID (command palette, log/diagnostic rows, plot series, annotations) use 0 for none. Gestures track their targets with flags, so a 0 ID still drags and selects. Keep one state object per view. Wheel zoom and pan keep ranges usable: a step that would overflow a log axis or shrink a span below what its magnitude resolves (|value| x 1e-12) is ignored. Selection ranges are reported ordered (min <= max). ArrayView and callbacks borrow data for the call; keep it alive while drawing. Curve points are finite and sorted by time; timeline durations are positive. Units, snapping policy, graph types and interpolation belong to the host. Editors return Edit<T> proposals with begin , update , commit , cancel . Atomic actions may return commit directly. Preview state never mutates the host. Validate and apply a committed proposal as one Undo transaction. Increment the supplied revision when replacing host data during a gesture to cancel stale edits. Ordinary rendering and model preparation run on the host UI thread. LogBuffer append/clear/snapshot are synchronized and may be called from producer threads. Colors use palette roles; UI geometry uses dp/style. Gradient colors, plot values, textures and scene matrices are application data. No module reads projects, executes Git actions, starts a terminal process, decodes audio/video, computes FFTs or runs a language server. Clipboard actions are local UI requests. Web explicitly creates a browser only when selected. Prepare documents/envelopes when data changes. Draw visible rows using cached models, and supply visible/bounded datasets for graphs and timelines. Plots accept at most 65,536 points per series by default and report oversized IDs in skippedSeries ; call reducePlot or query a host index before drawing. Heatmaps bound the displayed cells to 256 per axis. Diff uses patience anchors and bounded LCS (4 million cells by default), exposing approximate() when an unmatched region is displayed as a full replacement. Both source sides are retained; CRLF and LF lines compare equal and a notice row reports differing line endings. Source/Markdown inputs are limited to 32 MiB; large files need host paging. Logs default to 10,000 rows / 8 MiB. Waveforms consume prepared min/max envelopes. Python # sh Copy python -m pip install -e ".[ui]" cyui remains the existing theme/widget API. cyui_modules contains optional audio , canvas , plots , curves , nodes , timeline , audioviews , code , diff , inspector , assets , images , viewport , commands , diagnostics , documents ( documentviews alias), web and cef . Import models without loading imgui-bundle; drawing imports it lazily. No NumPy, media decoder or 3D engine is required. Python uses the same IDs, ranges, palette roles, edit phases, origin policy and bounded diff algorithm. Its CodeEditor uses ImGui multiline editing with native Undo and a live syntax preview. The richer C++ TextEditor backend has its own API; Python does not pretend to expose its multiple cursors/completion hooks. cyui_modules.cef.CEFRuntime loads the optional C ABI library/helper explicitly; CEF binaries are not included in the Python package. See WEB.md . Paged documents # CodePaging.h belongs to Code (C++17); PagedCodeEditor.h belongs to CodeEditor (C++20). The provider guide specifies bounded reads, UTF-16 positions, contextual syntax and host-owned transactions. The paged editor does not inherit the classic lexer's 32 MiB snapshot limit or copy the whole file. Per-page and input budgets still apply. This native C++ API has no Python or Web binding yet. Source packaging includes it when CodeEditor is selected; Unreal Editor compilation and platform input still require host validation. Native Markdown guide . Editor tools # Typed Inspector JSON, expressions, hierarchies, tables, file picker, commands and graph/timeline editing . set(CYUI_IMGUI_TARGET app_imgui) set(CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE) set(CYUI_BUILD_AUDIO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE) set(CYUI_BUILD_GALLERY OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE) set(CYUI_MODULES "Code;Diff;Inspector" CACHE STRING "" FORCE) add_subdirectory(external/CyUI) target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE CyUI::Diff CyUI::Inspector) #include <cyui/Core.h> #include <cyui/modules/Diff.h> #include <cyui/modules/Inspector.h> python -m pip install -e ".[ui]"

pages.title: Native Markdown, editing and media
pages.description: Compose native documents, chats and editors with optional resource adapters.
pages.html:
Try the standalone playground#

The SDL3 application shares its sources on Windows, Linux and macOS. Build with CMake using CYUI_BUILD_MARKDOWN_DEMO=ON and CYUI_BUILD_DEMO=OFF, then run cyui_markdown_test. On Windows, build_markdown_demo.bat provides a shortcut with Visual Studio 2022 and CMake, producing build\cyui_markdown_test.exe. CYUI_BUILD_PORTABLE_DEMO=ON also builds the SDL3 widget gallery cyui_demo_sdl3. SDL3 is example-only: installed >= 3.4, otherwise a pinned SHA-256-verified fetch; CYUI_FETCH_DEMO_DEPENDENCIES=OFF requires a local installation. The chat uses Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line, small hover/context copy/edit/reply/delete actions, and inline editing (Enter saves, Escape cancels). Use +, file-manager drop, or Ctrl+V (Cmd+V on macOS) to attach real files/images. Attachment-only messages work. Images enlarge in a native zoom view; Markdown/text attachments open in the document editor; the download icon saves a file.

The document defaults to Live direct rich editing, with compact/floating formatting, Source, Side by side and Reading modes. Images can be pasted, inserted or dropped, and relative paths resolve from the document's folder. Saving creates plain .md with referenced media in assets/; no CyMD package is needed. Ctrl+O opens, Ctrl+S saves, Ctrl+Shift+S saves as. English/French, five themes and both densities are available. The local chat is temporary.

Image import uses portable stb codecs (PNG/JPEG/BMP/TGA/PSD/GIF; first GIF frame). SDL3 handles windows, native rendering, file dialogs and drops. Clipboard images, HTML and copied files use SDL MIME data and isolated Windows/macOS adapters; macOS TIFF screenshots are converted to PNG. Paths and arguments remain UTF-8. File dialogs are asynchronous and their results reach app state on the UI thread. Web/CEF, YouTube, remote image fetching and link previews are optional separate services, with no runtime dependency here. --self-test checks messages, edit/cancel/reply, image decoding and a real document-plus-image file round trip. python tests/capture_markdown_demo.py captures the native views. CMake users can enable CYUI_BUILD_MARKDOWN_DEMO=ON.

Native message interaction#

TranscriptAttachment carries a stable ID, name, source, byte count and image flag. The host owns the bytes and supplies cached textures through DocumentServices. TranscriptMessage::own=false hides edit/delete; edited displays its status and replyTo links to another stable message ID. Hover/right-click actions return requests in TranscriptResult: edit, erase, reply, attachmentMessage, attachmentIndex and download. The renderer never edits host messages or opens files. Chat supports Discord underline __text__; document Markdown semantics stay unchanged and code spans/fences retain literal underscores.

cpp
cyui::MessageComposerState input;// Keep this state between frames. The host imports clipboard files/images.cyui::MessageComposerOptions options;options.canSubmitEmpty = !pendingAttachments.empty();auto action = cyui::messageComposer("message", input, {}, options);if (action.submitted) {    sendLocalMessage(input.text, pendingAttachments);    input.text.clear();    input.focus = true;}

paste(replacement) returns true when the host handled rich paste; an empty replacement is valid after importing attachments. TranscriptOptions::editing and editor(message,width) draw a host-owned editor inside a message row. Use the same composer with editing=true; save/cancel only on the returned requests. Formatting and native text selection remain available. No file dialog, network transport or browser engine is pulled into the reusable module.

Virtualize large conversations#

transcript renders and parses only visible message rows. Variable heights use a sparse index with logarithmic lookup/update; unseen rows start with an estimate. Logical scrolling uses double precision and a 64-bit scrollbar, with local drawing coordinates. The parsed-document/interaction cache defaults to 128 messages (cacheMessages), plus visible rows and pinned editors/open images. Height metadata contains no message text. A single visible message is still rendered as one document.

For a paged history, use TranscriptSource instead of allocating the whole message array:

cpp
cyui::TranscriptSource history;history.id = conversationId;history.count = store.messageCount();history.revision = store.orderRevision();history.message = [&](std::size_t row) { return pageCache.find(row); }; // pointer or nullptrhistory.request = [&](std::size_t first, std::size_t count) { queuePageRead(first, count); };history.indexOf = [&](cyui::ItemId id) { return store.indexOf(id); }; // indexed lookup, npos if absentcyui::transcript("history", state, history, {0, 500});

Callbacks run on the UI thread: queue I/O and publish loaded pages from the host. Unloaded rows show placeholders. prefetchRows requests a margin around the viewport. Increment revision after prepend/reorder/removal; appending only changes count. scrollToIndex, scrollTo, jumpToBottom and follow control navigation; public firstVisible/lastVisible and fetched expose the processed window. An uncached reply parent retains its ID jump link. The array overload uses the same virtual renderer; only an explicit ID jump may scan its array. Supply an indexed indexOf for large stores.

The gallery includes an on-demand million-message history. The standalone app can open the same stress case with --scenario million-chat, without allocating that history.

Choose the components#

The document reader and editor draw native Dear ImGui widgets and textures. Neither needs a browser. Select only the targets your application uses:

Target Purpose Dependencies
CyUI::DocumentViews Markdown reader and streaming transcripts Code, Images, MIT MD4C parser
CyUI::DocumentEditor Live, source, split and reading modes DocumentViews, CodeEditor, DataGrid
CyUI::DocumentIO In-memory .md/.cymd, clipboard HTML conversion DocumentViews, MIT miniz inflate
CyUI::Media Native audio/video playback controls Images; application playback backend
CyUI::DocumentWeb Optional document embed adapter DocumentViews, Web; application browser backend
cmake
set(CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_AUDIO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_GALLERY OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_MODULES "DocumentEditor;DocumentIO" CACHE STRING "" FORCE)add_subdirectory(external/CyUI)target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE CyUI::DocumentEditor CyUI::DocumentIO)

This selection does not compile Web, CEF, Media or load a codec. Rebuild consumers after updating the headers: the expanded models change the native binary ABI. The APIs use UTF-8 byte positions at codepoint boundaries. Keep one state per view.

Read and interact#

Document::setMarkdown parses only changed text. The reader supports nested emphasis, bold, underline (<u>), strikethrough, ==highlight==/<mark>, <kbd>, inline/fenced/indented code, quotes, ordered/nested lists, GFM tasks, aligned tables with escaped pipes, reference links, heading anchors, bare HTTP(S) URLs, numeric/named entities and Discord-style ||spoilers||. Unrecognized HTML is shown as text. It does not implement HTML/CSS layout or execute scripts.

cpp
#include <cyui/modules/DocumentViews.h>cyui::Document document;cyui::DocumentState view;document.setMarkdown("# Notes\n\n- [ ] Review\n\n||Reveal me||\n");auto result = cyui::documentView("notes", view, document, {0, 420});if (result.taskOffset != std::string::npos) {    auto source = document.markdown();    source[result.taskOffset] = result.taskChecked ? 'x' : ' ';    document.setMarkdown(source);}// result.link and result.media are requests for application policy/actions.

Drag text to select it and use Ctrl+C to copy visible text. Spoilers stay out of the selectable text until revealed. Internal links navigate to the generated heading anchor; DocumentState::jumpTo also requests an anchor. The state exposes reading positions. Tasks return exact source offsets, rather than silently changing an application's document. Transcripts reuse this renderer and cache messages by their stable IDs, including streamed Markdown.

Native images and optional embeds#

DocumentServices::image(source) returns cached ImageData. PNG, JPEG, SVG, GIF or another format is decoded by the application's native image pipeline; CyUI draws the resulting texture itself. An animated image may return a changing frame. No HTML image element or browser is involved. The host owns texture lifetimes and loading; the provider runs on the UI thread and must not block.

cpp
cyui::DocumentServices services;services.image = [&](const std::string& source) {    return cachedNativeImages.resolve(source); // application-owned ImageData};cyui::DocumentOptions options;options.services = &services;auto result = cyui::documentView("notes", view, document, {0, 420}, options);

Images preserve their aspect ratio. ![caption|320x180](assets/photo.png) supplies logical size bounds. Activate an image to enlarge it inside the application; the native viewport supports zoom/pan, and Escape closes it. The editable Live view includes a width grip. A read-only view can enable resizeImages and handle the returned resizedImage/resizedWidth proposal itself.

Image syntax pointing to a known audio/video extension creates a native fallback card. DocumentServices::embed is called only after user activation. A missing backend leaves the fallback usable. Cached DocumentLinkPreview objects supply title, description, thumbnail and optionally an embed URL/kind. Angle-bracket URLs suppress preview cards. Providers control resource access, network policy and cache storage; the renderer does not fetch remote content.

mediaPlayer accepts a MediaBackend: snapshots provide frames and playback state, and native controls request play/pause, seek, mute and volume. The same backend may be used elsewhere in the app. It does not decode a file or open an audio device. Seek is committed on release.

For web embeds, assign services.embed to a DocumentWebAdapter::draw callback. Its backend callback returns an existing WebBackend for the stable media ID. This may be a CyUI CEF view or the application's own adapter. The adapter navigates on URL/backend changes and reports web events. The application owns policy, backend lifetime, initialization and frame pumping, including hidden panels; follow the Web lifecycle. No second engine is created.

Edit a document#

cpp
#include <cyui/modules/DocumentEditor.h>cyui::DocumentEditor editor;editor.setMarkdown("# Notes\n\nSome **formatted text**.\n");cyui::DocumentEditorOptions options;options.document.services = &services;if (editor.draw("editor", {0, 560}, options).changed)    markDocumentDirty(editor.markdown());

Live uses native text inputs with Markdown markers hidden and styled glyphs overlaid at the input's own wrapping/selection positions. Images and tables are native elements. Code blocks are editable with lexical colors. Tables use the shared native DataGrid: edit cells directly, select/copy/paste ranges, and insert/remove rows or columns from the context menu. Spreadsheet headers and the grid toolbar are hidden in documents. Cell input accepts inline Markdown; Reading renders that formatting. Table changes share the source undo history. Source uses CodeEditor; Split adds a source-position-synchronized preview. Reading uses the same reader. Switching modes preserves the source. All native editing modes share the source editor's transaction history.

The main/floating toolbars and commands cover bold, italic, underline, strike, spoiler, inline code, links, headings, lists, tasks, quotes and indentation. select(first,last), insert(markdown) and command(...) are available to host menus. The editor reports changes instead of saving files. Ctrl/Cmd+1–4 changes mode; common formatting shortcuts and find/replace are available. Live edits normalize the edited block's Markdown representation, while other blocks remain untouched. Ctrl+A selects the whole document, and dragging can cross paragraph boundaries. Enter creates paragraphs/continues lists; Shift+Enter inserts a line break inside the same block, preserving its style. Live writes these breaks as <br> so blank lines survive parsing, focus changes, saving and reloading, including headings and list items. Native layout includes the final empty line and uses the same wrapping as keyboard input; the caret is the native input caret. Typing keeps the caret collapsed, and the floating formatting toolbar opens only for a text selection. Live paragraphs have no input-field outline. Backspace joins adjacent paragraphs and arrows move the caret between them. Typed Markdown is recognized in Live. focus() requests native keyboard focus at the selected source caret. Blank fenced blocks, empty list items and code nested in quotes/lists are opened in Source to preserve their structure.

pasteRich imports clipboard HTML/images through host services and returns Markdown referencing registered resources. Ctrl+Shift+V keeps the normal plain paste path. Pasting an HTTP(S) URL over a selection creates a link. drop accepts the chosen ImGui payload type and returns imported Markdown; the application converts OS file-drop events to its payload or calls insert directly. No OS clipboard backend or file manager is loaded by this module.

spelling(markdown, language) is an optional cached provider. It returns UTF-8 source ranges and suggestions. Live underlines those ranges; the suggestions menu applies replacements through the same undo history. Set spellingRevision when the provider's results/dictionary change. No dictionary is bundled or selected silently. Read-only mode disables changes and suggestions.

Files, clipboard and HTML export#

decodeMarkdown/encodeMarkdown preserve UTF-8/UTF-16 LE/BE, BOM and the source's line endings. readCyMD/writeCyMD handle the document.md, assets/, previews.json archive layout. ZIP imports accept stored/DEFLATE entries; exports use stored entries. The interfaces consume/return memory buffers and never extract files to disk. Keep the returned assets and preview cache with the document.

Default limits: 64 MiB archive, 128 MiB expanded, 32 MiB per entry, 4096 entries. Traversal, duplicate paths, encrypted/unsupported entries, symlinks, checksum errors and budget violations are rejected. ZIP64 is unsupported. documentAssetPath helps validate host resource keys; still apply the application's filesystem policy.

markdownFromHtml converts common clipboard formatting, links, paragraphs, lists, simple tables and code. Scripts/styles are discarded. Its explicit image importer must register pasted resources. It is a clipboard conversion helper, not an HTML/CSS renderer. documentHtml exports escaped portable HTML without scripts or remote fetching; relative media references remain relative and must be distributed with it. documentPackageHtml(package, title) instead embeds referenced package assets as data URLs for a self-contained HTML file. Archive metadata is preserved in manifest.

Python and validation#

Python provides documents, documenteditor, documentio, documentweb and media. Parsing uses the pure Python MIT markdown-it-py and linkify-it-py dependencies; model imports do not load imgui-bundle, CEF or playback engines. Resource services and backend contracts mirror the C++ architecture. Python positions exposed by the document/editor models are UTF-8 byte offsets. Advanced C++ TextEditor callbacks and source-editor capabilities remain C++ APIs. The Python editor supports basic block editing, the four views and shared history; floating toolbars, spelling, image resizing, source find/replace, synchronized scrolling and reader drag-selection are currently C++ features.

The gallery shows the reader/transcript at tab 18, editor at tab 24 and a clearly identified simulated playback backend at tab 25. The CI matrix builds and runs the native apps on Windows/Linux/macOS (software rendering; Linux uses Xvfb). Local verification covers Windows. Real Linux/macOS desktop interaction, native IME, clipboard, dialogs, scaling and external engines need target validation; the configured CI alone does not establish a successful run.

See grids, paginated documents and Office formats for ODT/ODS and DOCX/XLSX support.
