Choose the components # The document reader and editor draw native Dear ImGui widgets and textures. Neither needs a browser. Select only the targets your application uses: Target Purpose Dependencies CyUI::DocumentViews Markdown reader and streaming transcripts Code, Images, MIT MD4C parser CyUI::DocumentEditor Live, source, split and reading modes DocumentViews, CodeEditor, DataGrid CyUI::DocumentIO In-memory .md / .cymd , clipboard HTML conversion DocumentViews, MIT miniz inflate CyUI::Media Native audio/video playback controls Images; application playback backend CyUI::DocumentWeb Optional document embed adapter DocumentViews, Web; application browser backend cmake Copy set ( CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE ) set ( CYUI_BUILD_AUDIO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE ) set ( CYUI_BUILD_GALLERY OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE ) set ( CYUI_MODULES "DocumentEditor;DocumentIO" CACHE STRING "" FORCE ) add_subdirectory ( external/CyUI ) target_link_libraries ( app PRIVATE CyUI::DocumentEditor CyUI::DocumentIO ) This selection does not compile Web, CEF, Media or load a codec. Rebuild consumers after updating the headers: the expanded models change the native binary ABI. The APIs use UTF-8 byte positions at codepoint boundaries. Keep one state per view. Read and interact # Document::setMarkdown parses only changed text. The reader supports nested emphasis, bold, underline ( ), strikethrough, ==highlight== / , , inline/fenced/indented code, quotes, ordered/nested lists, GFM tasks, aligned tables with escaped pipes, reference links, heading anchors, bare HTTP(S) URLs, numeric/named entities and Discord-style ||spoilers|| . Unrecognized HTML is shown as text. It does not implement HTML/CSS layout or execute scripts. cpp Copy # include cyui :: Document document ; cyui :: DocumentState view ; document . setMarkdown ( "# Notes - [ ] Review ||Reveal me|| " ) ; auto result = cyui :: documentView ( "notes" , view , document , { 0 , 420 } ) ; if ( result . taskOffset != std :: string :: npos ) { auto source = document . markdown ( ) ; source [ result . taskOffset ] = result . taskChecked ? 'x' : ' ' ; document . setMarkdown ( source ) ; } // result.link and result.media are requests for application policy/actions. Drag text to select it and use Ctrl+C to copy visible text. Spoilers stay out of the selectable text until revealed. Internal links navigate to the generated heading anchor; DocumentState::jumpTo also requests an anchor. The state exposes reading positions. Tasks return exact source offsets, rather than silently changing an application's document. Transcripts reuse this renderer and cache messages by their stable IDs, including streamed Markdown. Native images and optional embeds # DocumentServices::image(source) returns cached ImageData . PNG, JPEG, SVG, GIF or another format is decoded by the application's native image pipeline; CyUI draws the resulting texture itself. An animated image may return a changing frame. No HTML image element or browser is involved. The host owns texture lifetimes and loading; the provider runs on the UI thread and must not block. cpp Copy cyui :: DocumentServices services ; services . image = [ & ] ( const std :: string & source ) { return cachedNativeImages . resolve ( source ) ; // application-owned ImageData } ; cyui :: DocumentOptions options ; options . services = & services ; auto result = cyui :: documentView ( "notes" , view , document , { 0 , 420 } , options ) ; Images preserve their aspect ratio. ![caption|320x180](assets/photo.png) supplies logical size bounds. Activate an image to enlarge it inside the application; the native viewport supports zoom/pan, and Escape closes it. The editable Live view includes a width grip. A read-only view can enable resizeImages and handle the returned resizedImage / resizedWidth proposal itself. Image syntax pointing to a known audio/video extension creates a native fallback card. DocumentServices::embed is called only after user activation. A missing backend leaves the fallback usable. Cached DocumentLinkPreview objects supply title, description, thumbnail and optionally an embed URL/kind. Angle-bracket URLs suppress preview cards. Providers control resource access, network policy and cache storage; the renderer does not fetch remote content. mediaPlayer accepts a MediaBackend : snapshots provide frames and playback state, and native controls request play/pause, seek, mute and volume. The same backend may be used elsewhere in the app. It does not decode a file or open an audio device. Seek is committed on release. For web embeds, assign services.embed to a DocumentWebAdapter::draw callback. Its backend callback returns an existing WebBackend for the stable media ID. This may be a CyUI CEF view or the application's own adapter. The adapter navigates on URL/backend changes and reports web events. The application owns policy, backend lifetime, initialization and frame pumping, including hidden panels; follow the Web lifecycle . No second engine is created. Edit a document # cpp Copy # include cyui :: DocumentEditor editor ; editor . setMarkdown ( "# Notes Some **formatted text**. " ) ; cyui :: DocumentEditorOptions options ; options . document . services = & services ; if ( editor . draw ( "editor" , { 0 , 560 } , options ) . changed ) markDocumentDirty ( editor . markdown ( ) ) ; Live uses native text inputs with Markdown markers hidden and styled glyphs overlaid at the input's own wrapping/selection positions. Images and tables are native elements. Code blocks are editable with lexical colors. Tables use the shared native DataGrid: edit cells directly, select/copy/paste ranges, and insert/remove rows or columns from the context menu. Spreadsheet headers and the grid toolbar are hidden in documents. Cell input accepts inline Markdown; Reading renders that formatting. Table changes share the source undo history. Source uses CodeEditor; Split adds a source-position-synchronized preview. Reading uses the same reader. Switching modes preserves the source. All native editing modes share the source editor's transaction history. The main/floating toolbars and commands cover bold, italic, underline, strike, spoiler, inline code, links, headings, lists, tasks, quotes and indentation. select(first,last) , insert(markdown) and command(...) are available to host menus. The editor reports changes instead of saving files. Ctrl/Cmd+1–4 changes mode; common formatting shortcuts and find/replace are available. Live edits normalize the edited block's Markdown representation, while other blocks remain untouched. Ctrl+A selects the whole document, and dragging can cross paragraph boundaries. Enter creates paragraphs/continues lists; Shift+Enter inserts a line break inside the same block, preserving its style. Live writes these breaks as
so blank lines survive parsing, focus changes, saving and reloading, including headings and list items. Native layout includes the final empty line and uses the same wrapping as keyboard input; the caret is the native input caret. Typing keeps the caret collapsed, and the floating formatting toolbar opens only for a text selection. Live paragraphs have no input-field outline. Backspace joins adjacent paragraphs and arrows move the caret between them. Typed Markdown is recognized in Live. focus() requests native keyboard focus at the selected source caret. Blank fenced blocks, empty list items and code nested in quotes/lists are opened in Source to preserve their structure. pasteRich imports clipboard HTML/images through host services and returns Markdown referencing registered resources. Ctrl+Shift+V keeps the normal plain paste path. Pasting an HTTP(S) URL over a selection creates a link. drop accepts the chosen ImGui payload type and returns imported Markdown; the application converts OS file-drop events to its payload or calls insert directly. No OS clipboard backend or file manager is loaded by this module. spelling(markdown, language) is an optional cached provider. It returns UTF-8 source ranges and suggestions. Live underlines those ranges; the suggestions menu applies replacements through the same undo history. Set spellingRevision when the provider's results/dictionary change. No dictionary is bundled or selected silently. Read-only mode disables changes and suggestions. Files, clipboard and HTML export # decodeMarkdown / encodeMarkdown preserve UTF-8/UTF-16 LE/BE, BOM and the source's line endings. readCyMD / writeCyMD handle the document.md , assets/ , previews.json archive layout. ZIP imports accept stored/DEFLATE entries; exports use stored entries. The interfaces consume/return memory buffers and never extract files to disk. Keep the returned assets and preview cache with the document. Default limits: 64 MiB archive, 128 MiB expanded, 32 MiB per entry, 4096 entries. Traversal, duplicate paths, encrypted/unsupported entries, symlinks, checksum errors and budget violations are rejected. ZIP64 is unsupported. documentAssetPath helps validate host resource keys; still apply the application's filesystem policy. markdownFromHtml converts common clipboard formatting, links, paragraphs, lists, simple tables and code. Scripts/styles are discarded. Its explicit image importer must register pasted resources. It is a clipboard conversion helper, not an HTML/CSS renderer. documentHtml exports escaped portable HTML without scripts or remote fetching; relative media references remain relative and must be distributed with it. documentPackageHtml(package, title) instead embeds referenced package assets as data URLs for a self-contained HTML file. Archive metadata is preserved in manifest . Python and validation # Python provides documents , documenteditor , documentio , documentweb and media . Parsing uses the pure Python MIT markdown-it-py and linkify-it-py dependencies; model imports do not load imgui-bundle, CEF or playback engines. Resource services and backend contracts mirror the C++ architecture. Python positions exposed by the document/editor models are UTF-8 byte offsets. Advanced C++ TextEditor callbacks and source-editor capabilities remain C++ APIs. The Python editor supports basic block editing, the four views and shared history; floating toolbars, spelling, image resizing, source find/replace, synchronized scrolling and reader drag-selection are currently C++ features. The gallery shows the reader/transcript at tab 18, editor at tab 24 and a clearly identified simulated playback backend at tab 25. The CI matrix builds and runs the native apps on Windows/Linux/macOS (software rendering; Linux uses Xvfb). Local verification covers Windows. Real Linux/macOS desktop interaction, native IME, clipboard, dialogs, scaling and external engines need target validation; the configured CI alone does not establish a successful run. See grids, paginated documents and Office formats for ODT/ODS and DOCX/XLSX support. cyui::MessageComposerState input; // Keep this state between frames. The host imports clipboard files/images. cyui::MessageComposerOptions options; options.canSubmitEmpty = !pendingAttachments.empty(); auto action = cyui::messageComposer("message", input, {}, options); if (action.submitted) { sendLocalMessage(input.text, pendingAttachments); input.text.clear(); input.focus = true; } cyui::TranscriptSource history; history.id = conversationId; history.count = store.messageCount(); history.revision = store.orderRevision(); history.message = [&](std::size_t row) { return pageCache.find(row); }; // pointer or nullptr history.request = [&](std::size_t first, std::size_t count) { queuePageRead(first, count); }; history.indexOf = [&](cyui::ItemId id) { return store.indexOf(id); }; // indexed lookup, npos if absent cyui::transcript("history", state, history, {0, 500}); set(CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE) set(CYUI_BUILD_AUDIO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE) set(CYUI_BUILD_GALLERY OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE) set(CYUI_MODULES "DocumentEditor;DocumentIO" CACHE STRING "" FORCE) add_subdirectory(external/CyUI) target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE CyUI::DocumentEditor CyUI::DocumentIO) #include cyui::Document document; cyui::DocumentState view; document.setMarkdown("# Notes - [ ] Review ||Reveal me|| "); auto result = cyui::documentView("notes", view, document, {0, 420}); if (result.taskOffset != std::string::npos) { auto source = document.markdown(); source[result.taskOffset] = result.taskChecked ? 'x' : ' '; document.setMarkdown(source); } // result.link and result.media are requests for application policy/actions. cyui::DocumentServices services; services.image = [&](const std::string& source) { return cachedNativeImages.resolve(source); // application-owned ImageData }; cyui::DocumentOptions options; options.services = &services; auto result = cyui::documentView("notes", view, document, {0, 420}, options); #include cyui::DocumentEditor editor; editor.setMarkdown("# Notes Some **formatted text**. "); cyui::DocumentEditorOptions options; options.document.services = &services; if (editor.draw("editor", {0, 560}, options).changed) markDocumentDirty(editor.markdown());

pages.title: Grids, paginated documents and Office formats
pages.description: Native cell editing, worksheets, document pages and OpenDocument/Open XML exchange.
pages.html:
Choose the modules#

These C++ modules draw native Dear ImGui controls. They do not require an installed office application, a browser or a server. The host supplies file dialogs, storage and native image textures. The Python document APIs keep their documented scope; these new Office widgets and file APIs are currently C++ only.

Target Purpose Dependencies
CyUI::DataGrid Reusable editable cell grid Core
CyUI::Spreadsheet Worksheets, formula bar and calculation DataGrid
CyUI::RichDocument Native paginated rich document editor DocumentEditor, DataGrid
CyUI::OfficeIO Office file exchange in memory RichDocument, Spreadsheet, DocumentIO, MIT pugixml
cmake
set(CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_AUDIO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_GALLERY OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_MODULES "DataGrid" CACHE STRING "" FORCE)add_subdirectory(external/CyUI)target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE CyUI::DataGrid)

Choose OfficeIO instead when the application needs both document/spreadsheet formats. Its dependencies are linked automatically. Selecting DataGrid alone does not compile Markdown, the source editor, XML, ZIP, Web, CEF or a formula engine. Without CMake, add each selected module's .cpp, its dependencies and feature defines. OfficeIO additionally compiles third_party/pugixml/pugixml.cpp; DocumentIO compiles miniz as described in the native Markdown guide.

Edit cells and tables#

cpp
#include <cyui/modules/DataGrid.h>cyui::GridModel cells(20, 6);cyui::GridState selection;cells.paste({0, 0}, "Item\tCount\nTexture\t4");if (cyui::dataGrid("inventory", selection, cells, {0, 420}).changed)    markDirty();

Click/Shift-click or drag to select a rectangular range. Arrows move the current cell; Shift extends the range. Double-click, F2 or Enter starts editing. Enter commits and moves down; Tab/Shift+Tab commits and moves between cells; Escape cancels the draft. Ctrl/Cmd+C/V copies/pastes a TSV grid. Quoted cells preserve embedded tabs, quotes and line breaks. Programmatic copy/paste also accept CSV with a comma separator; they do not execute cell text.

Use the toolbar/context menu to add, insert or remove rows and columns. Formatting supports bold, italic, underline/strike data, alignment and decimal precision. Columns resize with native table handles; their widths are view state, not an Office layout model. Models support atomic paste/structure edits and undo/redo. Read-only views do not change the model. Application data remains under host control.

Live Markdown tables reuse this grid and the document's source history. Their cells accept inline Markdown; Reading shows the formatted result. Markdown does not encode workbook formulas, page properties or arbitrary cell formatting.

Worksheets and formulas#

cpp
#include <cyui/modules/Spreadsheet.h>cyui::Workbook workbook;cyui::SpreadsheetState view;auto& sheet = workbook.sheets[0];sheet.name = "Budget";sheet.grid.setText(0, 0, "12.5");sheet.grid.setText(0, 1, "4");sheet.grid.setText(0, 2, "=A1*B1");cyui::spreadsheet("budget", view, workbook, {0, 480});

The formula bar edits the original cell text while the grid displays calculated values. Add, rename or close sheet tabs; workbook undo covers grid edits and structure changes. Native internal copy/paste retains cell types/formats and translates relative A1 references, preserving $A$1, $A1 and A$1 anchors. External clipboard input is plain TSV and cannot preserve rich cell metadata.

The bounded evaluator supports arithmetic + - * / ^, comparisons, concatenation &, percentages, A1 references/ranges, quoted sheet names, cross-sheet references, SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, COUNT, COUNTA, IF, ABS and ROUND. Function names use English, independent of the interface language. OpenFormula references/separators are translated for ODS/FODS exchange. Structural row/column edits shift references; deleted referenced cells become #REF!.

Cycles, division by zero, unknown functions and calculation limits are visible errors. Unknown formula source is retained for another spreadsheet application. The evaluator does not implement the complete Excel/OpenFormula function catalog, array formulas, named ranges, dynamic spill, external data or macros.

Paginated rich documents#

cpp
#include <cyui/modules/RichDocument.h>cyui::RichDocumentEditor editor;auto document = cyui::richDocumentFromMarkdown("# Report\n\nSome **rich text**.");document.page.leftMM = 24;document.page.header = "Project report";document.page.footer = "Page {page} / {pages}";editor.setDocument(document);if (editor.draw("report", {0, 640}))    saveDraft(editor.document());

Pages use physical dimensions and margins, native text wrapping, paragraph sizes, alignment, line spacing, images, tables, explicit page breaks and header/footer page fields. The workspace zoom does not change saved physical dimensions. Double-click a paragraph, table or image to open its native block editor. Paragraph editing reuses DocumentEditor; table editing reuses DataGrid. Apply commits one document transaction; Cancel discards that block draft. Host actions can use selectBlock, editBlock, setZoom, undo and redo.

This is a block-based paginated workspace. It does not provide a continuous text selection/caret across pages. Native pagination uses the current host font, so it does not promise the exact line/page breaks of Writer or Word. Table rows use a compact preview; large/multiline cell contents remain editable in the grid. Column widths normalize in Office output. Markdown conversion is a convenience and cannot retain page settings. Use the rich model and an Office format for that.

Exchange LibreOffice and Microsoft files#

Content Read/write formats
Rich documents ODT, DOCX, flat FODT
Workbooks ODS, XLSX, flat FODS

ODT/ODS are OpenDocument formats used by LibreOffice Writer/Calc. DOCX/XLSX use Open XML. Template extensions can be recognized for importing their content; these writers produce ordinary documents, not template packages. Legacy binary DOC/XLS, RTF, ODP/PPTX, encryption and password-protected files are unsupported.

cpp
#include <cyui/modules/OfficeIO.h>auto imported = cyui::readOfficeDocument(fileBytes, cyui::OfficeFormat::odt);showConversionIssues(imported.issues);editor.setDocument(imported.document);std::vector<cyui::OfficeIssue> issues;auto output = cyui::writeOfficeDocument(editor.document(),    cyui::OfficeFormat::docx, &issues);

Workbooks use readOfficeWorkbook/writeOfficeWorkbook with ods or xlsx. Text, common direct emphasis, basic paragraph/page properties, plain header/footer fields, editable rectangular tables, packaged images, sheet names, cell text/types, common formats and formula source have native representations. ODT/DOCX package image bytes are returned in document.assets; register them with a native image provider using their resource keys. No resource is extracted or fetched automatically. Flat FODT image export reports an issue; use packaged ODT for embedded images.

Inspect OfficeIssue before saving a converted file. Recognized unsupported features include named Word style definitions, arbitrary typography, merged cells, complex numbering, revision history, comments/notes, charts, pivots, external links and embedded objects. Some are flattened to visible values/text; others are omitted. OfficeOptions::strict = true rejects recognized lossy conversion. The issue list documents detected gaps, not a guarantee of complete fidelity. Keep the original when an application requires lossless editing of arbitrary files.

Limits and verification#

Grid limits: 100000 rows, 256 columns, one million cells, 32 MiB text and 1 MiB per cell. Workbooks accept at most 64 sheets and one million total cells. Dense models are intended for UI tools, not the entire address space of an Excel workbook. Imported repeated trailing empty ODF rows/columns are trimmed to the used range. Histories are bounded; very large snapshots may exceed the undo budget.

OfficeIO reuses DocumentIO's ZIP budgets (64 MiB archive, 128 MiB expanded, 32 MiB/entry, 4096 entries), rejects DTDs, limits XML depth/nodes and never resolves external entities. Formula parsing/dependency traversal have explicit budgets. The Office application used for validation is not a runtime dependency.

powershell
build_demo.batbuild\cyui_demo.exe --gallery-only --tab 26 --locale enctest --test-dir build/office-final --output-on-failurepython -B tests/validate_office_interop.py --exe build/office-final/cyui_test_office.exe

Native tests cover cell typing, clipboard parsing, transactions, formula references, cycles, formatting, pagination, block editing and all six file roundtrips. The optional interop script exchanges synthetic files through installed LibreOffice with an isolated profile, then checks text, tables, page fields and calculated totals. Windows and the installed LibreOffice are exercised locally. Linux/macOS runtime, Unreal Editor and arbitrary third-party document fidelity still require target testing.

References: OpenDocument 1.3 schema, SpreadsheetML sheets.

pages.title: CyUI manual
pages.description: A common Dear ImGui foundation for C++ and Python desktop tools.
pages.html:
CyUI is a themed widget library on top of Dear ImGui 1.92+, with independently selectable C++ and Python interface modules. It serves developers of editors, creative tools and desktop utilities who need consistent controls, localization and specialized views. The host application keeps its renderer, data, engines and Undo history.

Start here#

  • Integrate CyUI with your existing ImGui target.
  • Choose modules and follow the shared edit contract.
  • Explore Core widgets, module recipes, localization and quick filters.
  • Use Python, Web/CEF or the optional Unreal Editor connector.
  • Read licensing before redistributing dependencies.

Explore the demo#

Extract the entire portable Windows ZIP, then run cyui_demo.exe. English is the default; Launch-French.cmd selects French. The gallery has live theme, density and language choices. Samples use synthetic data and generated preview textures. Its mixer, transport and project panels illustrate UI; they are not an audio engine, project system or complete editor.

sh
cyui_demo.exe --locale frcyui_demo.exe --theme violet --comfortablecyui_demo.exe --gallery-only --tab 21cyui_demo.exe --gallery-only --tab 22cyui_demo.exe --gallery-only --tab 23cyui_demo.exe --gallery-only --tab 7 --image-graph

The native gallery contains Text, Buttons, Controls, Containers, Canvas, Plots, Curves, Nodes, Timeline, Audio views, Audio analysis, Spectral displays, Code, Diff, Details, Assets, Images, Viewport, Commands, Diagnostics, Documents, Web, Layout and Filtering. The Web page needs a separately configured CEF backend for live browsing; the ordinary downloadable demo does not bundle CEF or Unreal.

Platforms and status#

The current version is 1.2.0. The project does not declare an alpha/beta label; development is active.

Component Availability
Core and ordinary C++ modules Portable sources for Windows/Linux/macOS; local MSVC build/render validation on Windows, cross-platform CI configured
Standalone demo Windows x64, Win32/DirectX 11; no Linux/macOS demo binary
Python Python 3.10+, imgui-bundle for drawing; model imports are renderer-independent
CEF adapter Optional SDK/runtime; Windows validated locally, Linux/macOS deployment requires target validation
Unreal connector Optional UE 5.5+ Editor C++; local UE 5.8.4 Windows validation, other targets require validation

Core is C++17. CodeEditor and the tested CEF SDK integration require C++20. The Windows demo uses system fonts; portable hosts supply fonts covering their languages. See integration and localization limits.

Read offline#

Open Documentation/Documentation.html directly from disk. Keep the complete Documentation folder together, including DocData. There is no server, CDN, account or Internet dependency. Optional reference links to external projects require a connection only when you choose to follow them.

F1 and Help → Documentation in the demo open this local manual in the current interface language. The Help menu also opens the module, filtering and localization chapters. In the Python gallery, use the Documentation button or F1 for the active module. Help integration describes the reusable Python helper and native routes.

Use the sidebar and its nested topics, or Ctrl+K to search prose, code and documented API symbols. A language change keeps page and explicit section IDs. Images and galleries enlarge inside the documentation window; Escape closes the enlarged view. Keyboard focus exposes controls, touch controls remain available, and session navigation retains reading positions. Personal annotations/preferences depend on the browser’s local storage permissions.

Explore the illustrated module tour.

pages.title: Paged code editor
pages.description: Reusable virtual editing with host-owned storage, revisions and transactions.
pages.html:
CyUI::Code owns CodePaging.h: UTF-16 positions, bounded UTF-8 fragments, validation and a streaming line builder. CyUI::CodeEditor owns PagedCodeEditor.h, also included by CodeEditor.h. It draws and edits a virtual document without passing a page to the whole-document TextEditor backend. There is no dependency on CyCodeCore, a filesystem, MCP or a language server.

Select the component#

cmake
set(CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_AUDIO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_GALLERY OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_MODULES "CodeEditor" CACHE STRING "" FORCE)set(CYUI_IMGUI_TARGET app_imgui)add_subdirectory(external/CyUI)target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE CyUI::CodeEditor)

Use C++20 and one compatible ImGui instance. Code alone remains C++17. No extra runtime dependency is introduced. Unreal source packaging includes the new sources when CodeEditor is selected. This change supplies native C++ APIs; Python/Web virtual-editor bindings are not provided.

Host and view contract#

Keep one PagedCodeEditor per view on its ImGui/UI thread. Supply a PagedCodeDocument with a stable nonzero document ID, nonzero content revision, logical line count and read-only state. An empty source has one logical line; a final newline adds an empty final line. Revisions are equality guards, not timestamps. A different document/revision cancels stale reads and interactions.

Request and edit IDs are local to each view. Route asynchronous responses and acknowledgements to the originating view; include an application view key when batching requests from multiple editors of the same document.

draw returns a PagedCodeRead once when a new viewport needs data. The request contains its own ID, document/revision guards, a line interval, display-cell window, tab width and byte budget. Prepare it outside drawing, optionally in an application-owned worker. Deliver supplyPage on the UI thread. A response from an old request, document or revision is rejected. cancelledRead lets the host cancel its own superseded task. No worker or I/O is started by the widget.

Return one PagedCodeLine for every requested logical line, with full-line UTF-16/display-cell metrics and only its bounded visible fragment. The validator checks identity, coverage, UTF-8 boundaries, token spans and budgets. Missing or failed data is shown as loading/unavailable, with explicit Retry. The view uses 64-bit logical scroll origins and normalized scrollbars rather than an enormous floating-point ImGui canvas; precise line navigation remains integer-based.

cpp
cyui::PagedCodeEditor view; // persist with this panelview.setDocument({documentId, contentRevision, logicalLines, 0, readOnly});// Each frame:auto result = view.draw("##source", cyui::dp(0, 400));if (result.read) host.queueVisiblePage(*result.read);if (result.edit.committed()) host.applyGuardedReplacement(result.edit.value);for (const auto& action : result.actions) host.handleCodeAction(action);// Completed host reads are delivered to view.supplyPage(...) on the UI thread.

These host names illustrate responsibilities, not another required library. Use pendingRead, failRead and retryRead for an asynchronous adapter.

Coordinates and long lines#

Positions are zero-based logical lines and UTF-16 code units. They are distinct from UTF-8 byte offsets, display cells and tabs. Fragments exclude line endings and an initial file BOM; the host preserves all original source bytes. Tokens use fragment-local UTF-8 byte offsets and semantic palette roles.

PagedCodeLineBuilder accepts arbitrary UTF-8 chunk boundaries while scanning a single logical line. It retains only the requested horizontal fragment and calculates total UTF-16/display-cell metrics. It can resolve a requested UTF-16 position to revealedColumn() / revealedByte(), rejecting a split surrogate. A position past a shortened line clamps to its end. For a reveal read, retain the requested horizontal window when it already shows that position; otherwise return a window containing it and set page.firstColumn accordingly.

Display uses one cell per BMP scalar, two per supplementary scalar and configured tab stops. The default tab size is four. Wide/combining-script shaping, bidi, grapheme-cluster motion and soft wrapping are not implemented. The monospace font, palette roles, per-view Ctrl-wheel zoom and host DPI/style are shared with Code.

The byte budget applies to each page, not the whole file: at most 4 MiB, 4,096 requested rows, 8,192 display columns, 64 KiB per line fragment and 65,536 tokens. Input intents are bounded to 256 events and the configured insertion budget (1 MiB by default, at most 4 MiB). Exhaustion is explicit; it does not turn a partial fragment into a complete source document.

Edits and Undo ownership#

Typing, paste, Enter/Tab and deletion produce atomic EditPhase::commit replacement proposals containing the stable document ID, expected revision, ordered UTF-16 selection and UTF-8 replacement. The widget never changes the application's model or saves a file. Validate the proposal and commit one native Undo transaction, then call acceptEdit(id, newSnapshot, resultingSelection). The acknowledged revision must differ. Reject failure through rejectEdit.

Typing is queued behind an asynchronous edit; it is not discarded on each waiting frame. Rejection or an external revision cancels those intents and returns cancelledInput for host recovery, plus the cancelled edit proposal. Do not replay them silently on a different document. Complete or explicitly resolve pending input before destroying a view. After an external edit, the host may restore its rebased selection with setSelection.

Mouse selection reports begin/update/commit/cancel, with Escape cancellation. Basic arrows, Home/End, Page Up/Down and Ctrl/Cmd+A/Home/End are supported. Copy/Cut, Undo/Redo, Save and Find/next/previous are guarded host actions: the host can read selections across uncached pages, perform global search and own its clipboard/history. Copy the exact guarded selection before committing Cut. No second text Undo stack or viewport-only global search is created. Use keyboardShortcuts=false and requestAction for application keymaps.

For CyCodeCore, the application adapter translates these UTF-16 ranges to the Core's guarded byte/line operations and native Apply/Undo owner. It must supply page/line metrics and actual syntax context. The Core stays independent of CyUI. No Core/IDE/Reader adapter or paged LSP overlay is installed by this library change.

Syntax and example#

Supply token roles prepared with the real lexical/semantic context. Lexing an isolated fragment cannot infer an earlier multiline comment or embedded language. The existing highlightCode whole-snapshot limit and API are unchanged; this view does not secretly load or re-lex the entire source. Multiple cursors, folding, completion menus and word-level navigation are not part of this first paged view.

Gallery's Code page switches between the existing in-memory editor and Paged editor. Its small editable host demonstrates transactions, selection, clipboard and host Undo/Redo. A separate read-only million-line source generates only requested rows, including a streamed long line. It is synthetic demonstration data, not a benchmark of a million-line disk file.

text
build/cyui_demo.exe --gallery-only --tab 10 --paged-code --capture paged.bmp --theme navy

The standalone fixture's editable model is limited to 128 KiB; that is an example storage policy, not a document-size limit in the paged widget.

pages.title: Python integration
pages.description: Install the Python UI, import models and run the module gallery.
pages.html:
Installation#

CyUI requires Python 3.10+. Install the checkout with python -m pip install -e ., or install its built wheel. imgui-bundle 1.92+ is the declared drawing dependency; the historical [ui] extra remains compatible. Model-only imports under cyui_modules do not import the renderer, media decoders, NumPy or CEF.

python
from cyui_modules.common import Rangefrom cyui_modules.diff import DiffDocumentcomparison = DiffDocument()comparison.set_texts('old\n', 'new\n', 'plain')

Draw a gallery#

Run python examples/python_modules.py with imgui-bundle installed. Its ModuleGallery can also be embedded in your existing application. Create one gallery per host view, call draw during the GUI frame, and keep host textures/Web backends alive. Theme and language selectors update live; use the Documentation button or F1 for contextual help.

Use cyui.apply() once after context creation, cyui.set_locale('fr') for French, and cyui.render_notifications() once per frame. Follow the module edit recipes, translation scopes and filters.

Native and Python differences#

Python optional families use snake_case APIs. Its CodeEditor uses ImGui multiline editing, native Undo and a live syntax preview. The C++ TextEditor multiple cursors/completion hooks and native syntax-plugin registry are not Python bindings. Python SourceSpan offsets are UTF-8 bytes; displayed Python lexer spans use character indices. The Diff renderer is independent of the native C++ shared-canvas implementation.

CEF is explicitly loaded through CEFRuntime; its library, helpers and Chromium runtime are supplied separately. The Web guide explains thread, texture and shutdown ownership. The Python wheel includes the entire local manual as cyui_documentation package data; no Node.js is required to read it.

pages.title: Core recipes
pages.html:
Inspector panel

cpp
if (ImGui::Begin("Inspector")) {    cyui::panelHeader("Layer", layer.name.c_str());    cyui::divider();    if (cyui::beginSection("Transform")) {        if (cyui::beginProperties("##transform")) {            cyui::property("Position");  ImGui::DragFloat2("##pos", &layer.x);            cyui::property("Opacity");   cyui::sliderBar("##opacity", &layer.opacity, 0, 1, "%.2f", -1);            cyui::property("Visible");   cyui::toggleSwitch("##visible", &layer.visible);            cyui::property("Blend", "How the layer mixes with the ones under it.");            cyui::combo("##blend", &layer.blend, blendNames, blendCount);            cyui::endProperties();        }        cyui::endSection();    }}ImGui::End();

Tool palette

cpp
for (int i = 0; i < toolCount; ++i) {    if (cyui::iconButton(tools[i].icon, tools[i].tooltip, current == i))        current = i;    ImGui::SameLine(0, cyui::dp(2));}cyui::toolbarSeparator();

Confirm dialog

cpp
if (cyui::beginModal("Discard changes?", &askDiscard)) {    ImGui::TextWrapped("The project has unsaved changes.");    if (cyui::modalButtons("Discard", "Cancel", true) == 1)        discard();    cyui::endModal();}

Custom canvas colours

pages.title: Reusable CyUI module for Unreal plugins
pages.description: Reusable CyUI module for Unreal plugins for CyUI integrators.
pages.html:
CyUI is an optional Editor module that other Unreal plugins can embed or share. It supplies the CyUI/ImGui library, the Slate renderer, input, clipboard, font textures and Unreal texture registry. Loading the module creates no menus, demo tools or windows. Your plugin owns its layout, commands and state. Core/CMake/Python consumers do not acquire Unreal dependencies. This integration is for native C++ editor tools, not UMG, runtime gameplay UI or Blueprints.

Embed the module in an existing plugin#

Prepare a new staging directory (Python 3.10+):

sh
python tools/package_unreal.py --layout module --output build/unreal-module/CyUI --modules Core Plots Inspector Code Diff

module is the default layout. Copy that single CyUI folder to <YourPlugin>/Source/CyUI. It contains its Build.cs, public headers, private backend, selected library snapshot, dependencies and MIT notices. It requires no separate CyUI plugin and no external checkout path.

Append this entry to your plugin's existing .uplugin Modules array; the generated ModuleDescriptor.json contains the same entry. Keep your existing module entries:

json
{ "Name": "CyUI", "Type": "Editor", "LoadingPhase": "PostEngineInit" }

Add "CyUI" to the dependencies of your plugin's Editor module:

csharp
PrivateDependencyModuleNames.Add("CyUI");CppStandard = CppStandardVersion.Cpp20;

Use PublicDependencyModuleNames instead if your public headers expose CyUI types. Runtime/gameplay modules must not depend on this Editor module. Regenerate IDE project files and build the Editor target with UnrealBuildTool.

Inside the module, Library/src and third-party implementations retain their source bytes as .inl files. Generated .cpp bridges compile each exactly once; UBT's recursive source discovery cannot compile duplicate implementations. Header paths and the API remain unchanged. Library/SOURCE_LAYOUT.json records the original-to-packaged paths; the TextEditor hash manifest uses its packaged name. No engine code is copied. CYUI_API remains empty for static CMake integration.

A plugin you redistribute: unique module name#

Two enabled plugins that each embed a module named CyUI cannot load together: Unreal needs one definition per module name. A plugin distributed to others (a Marketplace/Fab or studio-wide tool) should therefore either depend on the shared provider plugin below, or embed a copy under its own module name:

sh
python tools/package_unreal.py --layout module --module-name MyToolCyUI --output build/unreal-module/MyToolCyUI --modules Core Plots

Copy the folder to <YourPlugin>/Source/MyToolCyUI, list { "Name": "MyToolCyUI", "Type": "Editor", "LoadingPhase": "PostEngineInit" } in your .uplugin and depend on "MyToolCyUI" in Build.cs. The script renames the Build.cs class/file, the folder, the descriptor and test names; the Build.cs defines CYUI_UNREAL_MODULE (used by IMPLEMENT_MODULE and FCyUIModule::Get()) and maps CYUI_API to MYTOOLCYUI_API. C++ class names and headers are unchanged.

Each embedded copy still contains its own Dear ImGui build and exports it (IMGUI_API=CYUI_API, public third_party/imgui include path). A consumer module must depend on exactly one CyUI module, and must not also use another ImGui plugin's headers. ImGui itself is not renamespaced: with two copies loaded, Windows keeps each DLL's symbols separate; Linux/macOS symbol resolution between two copies has not been validated.

Share one module between several plugins#

A project must contain one definition of the module named CyUI. To use several consumer plugins together, put the module in one common provider plugin and make the consumers depend on it. Do not copy Source/CyUI into each enabled plugin.

An optional provider container can be prepared with:

sh
python tools/package_unreal.py --layout plugin --output build/unreal-provider/CyUI --modules All --gallery

Copy it to <Project>/Plugins/CyUI. In each consuming plugin's .uplugin, append this reference to its existing Plugins array:

json
{ "Name": "CyUI", "Enabled": true }

The consumer's Build.cs still depends on the module CyUI. The provider plugin is only a container and adds no interface on its own. If your provider has a different plugin name, use that name in the Plugins reference; the module name in Build.cs remains CyUI (or the --module-name you packaged it with). Follow Unreal's project/engine dependency hierarchy.

--modules Core is minimal; All includes all ordinary CyUI modules. Dependencies are selected automatically. --gallery only includes the gallery API: your plugin chooses when to call it. CEF and external ImGuizmo are not packaged here. Existing output folders are refused. Prepare a new staging folder and replace the previous module deliberately with the editor closed. Restart after backend/library changes; the shared module disables dynamic unloading.

Complete consuming-plugin example#

examples/unreal/CyUIToolExample is a separate plugin with its own Build.cs, descriptor, Window-menu entry, nomad tab, Slate layout, CyUI draw callback and teardown. Its descriptor references the shared provider CyUI; enable this example only when you want its interface. It embeds a panel using MakePanel, not a stand-alone CyUI window. With Gallery selected, its own interface can open the gallery. For embedding in an existing plugin, copy the example's integration pattern and declare the module inside that plugin as described above.

Register an editor tool#

In your Editor module's .Build.cs:

csharp
PrivateDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new[] { "Core", "CyUI" });CppStandard = CppStandardVersion.Cpp20;

Register the tool in StartupModule, unregister it in ShutdownModule:

cpp
#include "CyUIModule.h"#include <cyui/Core.h> void FMyEditorTools::StartupModule(){    FCyUIModule::Get().RegisterTool(        "MyTools.Inspector", NSLOCTEXT("MyTools", "Inspector", "My CyUI Inspector"),        FOnDrawCyUITool::CreateRaw(this, &FMyEditorTools::DrawInspector));} void FMyEditorTools::DrawInspector(){    cyui::heading("My editor tool");    if (cyui::primaryButton("Inspect selection")) {        // Read the editor selection / request a host action here.    }} void FMyEditorTools::ShutdownModule(){    if (FCyUIModule::IsAvailable())        FCyUIModule::Get().UnregisterTool("MyTools.Inspector");}

RegisterTool rejects empty/duplicate IDs and unbound callbacks. OpenTool(id) opens the registered nomad tab. Your plugin adds its own menu/button/command to call OpenTool; the service does not add a Window menu. Unregistration detaches the callback before requesting tab closure, so a closed/unloading owner cannot keep drawing. For an existing Slate layout, MakePanel(callback) returns an SWidget. Keep the owning callback valid for its panel's lifetime; cast to SCyUIPanel and call Detach() before destroying a raw callback owner.

cpp
#include "CyUIModule.h"#include "SCyUIPanel.h" // During your toolkit/tab construction, keep this as an owning-plugin member:Panel = StaticCastSharedRef<SCyUIPanel>(FCyUIModule::Get().MakePanel(    FOnDrawCyUITool::CreateRaw(this, &FMyEditorTools::DrawInspector)));// Insert Panel.ToSharedRef() in a Slate slot or SDockTab content.// Before unloading the owning plugin:if (Panel) { Panel->Detach(); Panel.Reset(); }

CyUIModule.h exposes the FCyUIModule entry point. The older CyUIEditorModule.h / FCyUIEditorModule names remain compatible aliases/types.

Both methods accept an optional FOnInitializeCyUITool as their last argument. It runs once per newly created panel with its context current, after the default fonts are loaded and before the first frame. Use it to merge a host-supplied font into cyui::uiFont() (set ImFontConfig::MergeMode and DstFont) or configure additional fonts. SCyUIPanel exposes the same OnInitialize Slate argument. Unicode storage/input does not supply missing font glyphs: choose fonts covering the scripts your tool displays, with appropriate distribution rights.

The connector owns CreateContext, NewFrame, the root Begin/End, Render and notifications. The callback draws contents. Do not run another ImGui frame, destroy/change the context or load fonts from a draw callback. CyUI Gallery may create its own ordinary ImGui windows inside the panel. Native OS windows and docking belong to Slate; ImGui multi-viewport OS windows are disabled.

All APIs/callbacks run on the editor game thread. Work that changes assets or the world must use the owning Unreal tool's transactions, Modify, validation and Undo/Redo. Draw callbacks may run more than once per editor frame; execute actions on widget events rather than unconditionally. Read/prepare expensive data outside the paint callback.

Each panel owns an independent ImGui context. Numeric-entry buffers, wheel state and notifications are scoped to that context and released on context shutdown. Palette, density, DPI and fonts are per context too: a theme call styles the panel whose context is current (inside its draw/initialize callback), and a new panel starts from the defaults set by theme calls made while no ImGui context is current. From Slate handlers or other code outside the draw callback, use the panel helpers: Panel->RunInContext([] { cyui::setTheme("navy"); }), and Panel->Notify("Saved", cyui::Tone::success) (or cyui::notify(context, ...)). A plain cyui::notify() with no current context is dropped. Slate's render transform handles desktop DPI, while DisplayFramebufferScale supplies font rasterization density; the panel keeps CyUI's logical DPI at 1 and does not re-apply the style on every paint.

Input routing: each key goes to exactly one side. ImGui receives it (and Slate sees it handled) while ImGui takes keyboard input: an active item or text field, a modal, or a focused view that calls ImGui::SetNextFrameWantCaptureKeyboard(true) (as webPanel does); plain navigation keys (arrows, Tab, Space, Enter, Escape, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End) also go to ImGui while its keyboard navigation is active. Every other key goes only to Unreal, so editor shortcuts such as Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z, Delete or F7 work over the panel and never run twice. A tool with its own shortcuts (Delete, Ctrl+C/V in a canvas) must claim the keyboard that way while focused. Characters go to ImGui only while it takes keyboard input. The mouse wheel is sent as vertical; ImGui turns Shift+wheel into horizontal scrolling. ImGui's own textures (font atlas) are transient UTexture2Ds updated in place, only in the changed rectangle.

Show Unreal textures#

cpp
const uint64 imageId = FCyUIModule::Get().RegisterTexture(myTexture);// In the draw callback (or ImageData for CyUI::Images / Viewport):ImGui::Image(ImTextureRef(ImTextureID(imageId)), cyui::dp(256, 256));// After the tool stops submitting this image:FCyUIModule::Get().UnregisterTexture(imageId);

Registration holds a strong UObject reference. Unregistration finishes submitted Slate/render commands before releasing that reference; avoid doing it every paint. Register/unregister textures outside draw callbacks, after stopping submissions of the old image, for example in the owning tool's setup/teardown. ID 0 and stale/unregistered IDs are skipped. Texture IDs from other ImGui or RHI backends are not valid here. Only ordinary Slate-renderable UTexture resources are supported by this registry; custom GPU pipelines need their own adapter.

Compatibility and limits#

The connector targets Unreal Engine 5.5+ desktop editor builds on Windows/Linux/macOS through public Slate APIs. The locally validated installation is UE 5.8.4 on Windows x64. Other versions and platforms require validation on the target installation.

IME composition/candidate placement, accessibility text providers, touch/gamepad and OS-level ImGui multi-viewports are not implemented by this basic editor backend. Basic Unicode character events and clipboard text are supported. An existing third-party Unreal ImGui plugin may use a different ABI/context; do not share its headers, symbols or texture IDs with this connector.

The generic Web module may be selected, but WebCEF is not packaged into Unreal. Unreal may already load its own browser runtime; a Web backend for Unreal must follow that engine's browser lifecycle and version requirements.

CyUI's English/French localization is included through Core. Set the panel's language within RunInContext or its draw callback; separate panel contexts keep separate languages. Slate tool/menu entries still use Unreal localization. See LOCALIZATION.md for the catalog and stable-label API.

License#

CyUI's connector and packaging script remain MIT. Dear ImGui and the optional TextEditor retain their MIT notices. Unreal Engine remains an external dependency under Epic's own license; it is not redistributed or relicensed by CyUI. Preserve the plugin's LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES when distributing CyUI code.

pages.html:
CyUI's optional Web module embeds HTML/CSS/JavaScript interfaces in a Dear ImGui panel. TypeScript is compiled to JavaScript by the web application's own build. The supplied browser engine is CEF, using off-screen rendering into a texture owned by the host renderer. This avoids a platform-native child window covering ImGui popups or docking panels. No browser dependency enters Core.

Platform and validation matrix#

Component Windows Linux macOS
Core and ordinary C++ modules Portable sources; MSVC build/tests/render checked locally Portable sources; CI configured, not run locally Portable sources; CI configured, not run locally
Python models / imgui-bundle UI Models and real ImGui frames checked locally Same Python sources; target environment needs validation Same Python sources; target environment needs validation
Web policy, messages, JS/TS declarations Tested Platform-independent code Platform-independent code
WebCEF off-screen adapter Compiled; real page, paint and native/Python message round trips tested Shared implementation; build/runtime packaging unverified here Shared implementation; framework/helper/AppKit packaging unverified here
Win32/DX11 demo and BMP capture Implemented and tested Host supplies its ImGui backend Host supplies its ImGui backend

CEF itself supplies Windows, Linux and macOS distributions. CyUI does not claim that adding a CMake option validates a finished application on all three systems. CEF was tested here with 150.0.23+g4ccc4ca+chromium-150.0.7871.287, Windows x64. Choose and validate a maintained CEF SDK for each target architecture.

Build selection#

cmake
set(CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_MODULES "Web" CACHE STRING "" FORCE)set(CYUI_BUILD_WEB_CEF ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)set(CYUI_CEF_ROOT "path/to/extracted/cef_binary_distribution" CACHE PATH "" FORCE)add_subdirectory(external/CyUI)target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE CyUI::WebCEF)

Alternatively set CYUI_CEF_TARGET to a host target providing the CEF headers, runtime library and C++ wrapper. This is useful when the application already owns CEF packaging. The adapter requires C++20 for the tested SDK. Core remains C++17. No SDK/runtime download happens during configure or drawing.

The build also creates cyui_webcef_bridge (a C ABI shared library) and cyui_webcef_helper for optional Python/foreign hosts. A host already running CEF should use its own process/app integration rather than initialize a second runtime.

Native lifecycle#

  1. Pass cyui::webCEFApp() to both CefExecuteProcess and CefInitialize before creating views. Use the same renderer handler in all helper executables.
  2. Set CefSettings.windowless_rendering_enabled = true. The application owns CEF initialization, sandbox policy, cache/profile directory and subprocess paths.
  3. Supply an upload callback accepting an upper-left-origin BGRA8 buffer. Update a reusable host GPU texture and return its ImTextureID. The buffer expires after the callback. The texture remains host-owned. The optional release callback runs once, when the browser has closed, with the last texture returned by upload: the view no longer draws it. Free it only once no submitted frame references it (renderers with frames in flight defer by that many frames).
  4. Call CefDoMessageLoopWork() once per loop iteration outside the ImGui frame (before NewFrame, never between NewFrame and Render). upload and release run inside it, so texture updates and releases never race a draw list that is being built. Then NewFrame, beginFrame(), webPanel, endFrame(), Render. The end call hides an undrawn tab/panel.
  5. Call close() on all views and keep pumping until closed(). Destroy views before GPU resources, then call CefShutdown() on the initializing thread.

Every backend call must run on the CEF UI thread (the thread that called CefInitialize with the single-threaded loop). Calls from another thread are ignored and return false, construction throws; debug builds also assert.

cpp
#include <cyui/adapters/WebCEF.h> cyui::WebCEFOptions options;options.url = "http://127.0.0.1:4173/chat";options.policy.origins = {"http://127.0.0.1:4173"};options.upload = [&](int width, int height, const void* bgra) {    return renderer.updateBrowserTexture(width, height, bgra);};options.release = [&](ImTextureID texture) { renderer.releaseAfterFramesInFlight(texture); };auto web = cyui::createWebCEF(options); // after CefInitialize // Each host loop iteration, on the same thread:CefDoMessageLoopWork();       // outside the ImGui frameImGui::NewFrame();web->beginFrame();if (ImGui::Begin("Chat")) {    for (const auto& event : cyui::webPanel("##chat", *web, {0, 0})) {        if (event.kind == cyui::WebEventKind::navigated)            web->postJson(cyui::webThemeJson());        // Parse/validate application messages; apply host commands explicitly.    }}ImGui::End();web->endFrame();ImGui::Render();

The default software paint path bounds each view to 4096×4096 pixels and 30 fps; options allow limits up to 8192. HTML select popups are composited into the same texture. webPanel forwards mouse buttons (with the press's click count on release, so dblclick fires), both wheels, Unicode characters and keys: letters, digits, F1-F24, punctuation, keypad, navigation/editing keys and left/right modifiers. On Windows the adapter adds the active layout's scan code, so the page receives KeyboardEvent.code. While the panel is focused it owns those keys (ImGui key ownership): Tab, arrows, Space, Enter or Escape do not also move ImGui keyboard navigation or activate other widgets. WebPanelOptions::focus is one-shot: focus is taken when it changes from false to true, so a click elsewhere can still unfocus the page. The host must keep platform text input enabled while the backend is focused. Use webCEFBrowser() for platform-native key events, IME composition/candidate placement, accessibility, external file drag/drop or other advanced CEF integrations. These platform features are host responsibilities, not validated by the basic pointer/text/message tests.

CEF message pumping is intentionally single-threaded here. Do not enable CEF's multi-threaded message loop and then invoke this backend from a different ImGui thread. Background engine work stays in CEF's subprocesses.

Browser boundary#

WebPolicy accepts exact HTTP(S) origins, including ports. It rejects credentials, file/javascript URLs, wildcard matching, malformed ports and ambiguous backslashes. Use a loopback server for a built local frontend or an explicitly permitted HTTPS origin. CyUI does not start the frontend's server, compile TypeScript or choose its authentication. CEF retains normal browser networking for page subresources.

Main-frame navigation outside allowed origins and new-window requests (popups, target=_blank) are never opened by the adapter; they become external events. An external event is a request from page content, not a command:

  • Only schemes in WebPolicy::externalSchemes (default http, https) are reported; others (file:, ms-settings:, custom protocol handlers...) are dropped. Add a scheme only deliberately.
  • Popups from sub-frames (including cross-origin iframes) are dropped unless they come from a user gesture. Events carry userGesture, mainFrame and the requesting frame's sourceOrigin.
  • Before handing a URL to ShellExecute, open or a system browser, check it against your own scheme/host allow-list and ask the user to confirm. Never pass an event URL to the shell unchecked.

Messages are accepted only from the main frame of an allowed origin and are size checked before parsing. The page-side limit in the renderer follows maxMessageBytes (default 1 MiB, at most 64 MiB). Host messages (postJson) are bound to the origin loaded when they were sent: the renderer drops them if the page has navigated to another origin meanwhile. The event queue holds maxQueuedEvents (256); error/console events have a separate lower cap, maxQueuedErrors (16), so a noisy page cannot evict messages. Anything discarded (full queue, caps, oversized data, refused schemes or popups) is counted and reported by a dropped event whose data is the count. Downloads, media permissions and other permission prompts are denied by the supplied minimal adapter; enable product-specific capabilities in an explicitly reviewed host integration if required.

Process sandbox#

The supplied binaries run CEF without its process sandbox on Windows. Windows sandboxing needs sandbox information created by the executable's entry point; the cyui_webcef_bridge library and the generic cyui_webcef_helper pass none, so the bridge sets no_sandbox = true explicitly. A sandbox request (Python no_sandbox=False, the default) is reported, not honoured: cyui_cef_sandboxed() returns 0, cyui_cef_error() explains it, and CEFRuntime issues a RuntimeWarning and sets sandboxed = False. On Linux the request is passed to Chromium (which needs chrome-sandbox or user namespaces); on macOS the helper bundle must also initialize CefScopedSandboxContext. Neither is validated here.

To sandbox a Windows host with the tested CEF 150 SDK, use CEF's bootstrap layout (see the SDK's cef_sandbox_win.h and CEF's sandbox guide): ship bootstrap.exe (or bootstrapc.exe for console apps) renamed to your application, build the application and its subprocess entry as a DLL exporting RunWinMain / RunConsoleMain, and pass the sandbox_info it receives to both CefExecuteProcess and CefInitialize, with no_sandbox = false. Older SDKs that ship cef_sandbox.lib instead link it into the executable and create CefScopedSandboxInfo in wWinMain. The browser and every helper must use the same arrangement. Validate it on the target system before claiming sandboxing.

Browser JavaScript / TypeScript#

web/ is the MIT @cyui/web package with JavaScript, TypeScript declarations and an optional CSS stylesheet. CEF installs a narrow window.cyuiNative message transport. No Electron or Node API is exposed to the page.

ts
import {createCyUIBridge} from '@cyui/web';const bridge = createCyUIBridge();bridge.on('host.reply', payload => updateView(payload));bridge.send('chat.message', {text: 'Hello'});// Dispose listeners when the embedded UI is destroyed.bridge.close();

Messages contain {protocol: 'cyui.web', version: 1, type, payload, requestId?}. The application owns message schema, authorization and effects. A theme message from webThemeJson()/theme_message() supplies palette CSS variables such as --cyui-bg0, --cyui-text and --cyui-accent; send it again after a theme change. JSON is transported as data through CEF process messages, without interpolating host text as executable JavaScript.

Embedded web frontends#

mountCyMD() supports the existing version-1 iframe protocol: explicit parent origin, frame identity and session checks, ready/open/save/state messages, Blob documents and save acknowledgments. The host supplies onSave; CyUI does not write files. Native JSON does not transport Blob objects: handle document transfer in the host page, with a bounded host protocol when required. Web frontends retain their own services, licenses and adapters. Replace Electron preload/IPC dependencies with explicit host messages where needed.

Python#

python
from cyui_modules.cef import CEFRuntimefrom cyui_modules.web import web_panel, theme_message with CEFRuntime(library_path, helper_path, absolute_cache_path, no_sandbox=True) as runtime:    view = runtime.create(url, (allowed_origin,), upload_bgra_to_host_texture,                          release=release_texture_later)    # Each loop iteration:    runtime.pump()            # before new_frame: uploads/releases happen here    imgui.new_frame()    runtime.begin_frame()    events = web_panel('chat', view, (0, 400))    for event in events:        if event['kind'] == 'navigated':            view.post_json(theme_message())    runtime.end_frame()    imgui.render()

All runtime/view calls must run on the owning UI thread. begin_frame() does not pump; call pump() outside the ImGui frame. The context manager closes and pumps all views before shutting CEF down; shutdown fails while a view is alive, and CEF cannot be initialized again in the same process. An upload callback receives a native pointer valid only during the call; copy/update immediately. release runs from pump() after the view closed. no_sandbox=True states what the bridge does on Windows anyway (see Process sandbox); leaving the default warns. Python's garbage collector does not initialize or shut down a browser on an arbitrary thread.

Deployment and checks#

Native webThemeJson() and Python theme_message() also carry the current UI locale (English by default). Send a fresh theme after changing languages. The JavaScript bridge translates only marked interface elements and exposes a catalog for TypeScript components; see LOCALIZATION.md. Bundle the bridge's cyui-i18n.js and cyui-locales.js imports with the main bridge module.

  • Windows: ship matching libcef/Chromium runtime files, resources/locales, helper executable and supported sandbox setup. The optional test/demo CMake staging copies the selected SDK's Release/Resources into the build output.
  • Linux: ship/use matching libcef.so, resources/locales and helper; configure the runtime search path, target display stack and Chromium sandbox as CEF requires.
  • macOS: package/load Chromium Embedded Framework.framework and correctly named signed helper app bundles, integrate CEF's AppKit application handling, entitlements and sandbox setup. The generic helper source is not a complete macOS app bundle.
  • Keep the selected SDK's LICENSE.txt, CREDITS.html and other component notices. See LICENSING.md.

pages.title: Widget API reference
pages.description: Widget API reference for CyUI integrators.
pages.html:
All functions are in namespace cyui. The headers carry the full comments.

Units. Widget size and width parameters are screen pixels: wrap design values in dp(), as in cyui::button("OK", cyui::dp(80, 0)). 0 means automatic, and a negative width fills the row minus that much. These are design units, scaled inside:

  • beginCard height
  • beginProperties label width
  • beginSidebar and beginModal widths
  • space height, divider spacing, spinner radius
  • KnobStyle::diameter

beginTopBar's height is in pixels.

Disabled and edited. Inside ScopedDisabled, CyUI's hand-drawn widgets fade and stop reacting, like stock ImGui. Every CyUI control that changes a value marks it edited, so ImGui::IsItemEdited() is true after it on that frame. Clicks and drags also give ImGui::IsItemDeactivatedAfterEdit() on release: one undo step per gesture. Wheel nudges and typed values are one-shot edits that only set IsItemEdited(). markEdited(id) does the same for your own controls.

Theme (Theme.h)#

  • Setup: apply(Config), applyDpi(s), dpi() (the current scale), loadFonts(FontConfig).
  • Palette: palette(), setPalette(p), setTheme("key"), builtInThemes(), currentThemeKey(). paletteFields() lists each role with its key, label, group and member pointer, for editors and theme files.
  • Density and metrics: setDensity(d), density(), metrics(). The metrics give the font size, paddings, roundings, cardPadding and toolbarHeight.
  • Fonts: uiFont(), boldFont(), monoFont(), iconsAvailable(). The fonts are null until loadFonts filled the context's atlas. ScopedFont(nullptr, factor) then keeps the current font.
  • Colour helpers: rgb(0xRRGGBB, a), alpha, mix, brighter, darker, vec, categorical(i). categorical gives 12 hues derived from the palette, toned for light or dark grounds.
  • Sizes: dp(v) / dp(x, y).
  • Theme files: savePalette(path, p), loadPalette(path, p), paletteToText, paletteFromText. The .cytheme format is key = #RRGGBB[AA]; CyDAW's JSON .cytheme files also load.

Icons (Icons.h)#

cyui::icon::play, pause, stop, record, add, remove, trash, settings, search, folder, save, undo, redo, edit, close, check, chevronDown, more, refresh, zoomIn, lock, filter, loop, library, star, copy, paste, info, warning, home, globe, people, mail, calendar, clock, cloud, upload, download, code, photo, document, ... (104 icons). They are UTF-8 strings of Segoe MDL2 Assets, so they work in any label: std::string(icon::save) + " Save". They draw only on Windows. Without the icon font, the CyUI widgets fall back:

  • iconButton shows the first letter of its tooltip when the current font lacks the glyph (a host's own merged icon font still works).
  • iconTextButton shows the label alone.
  • sidebarItem and emptyState leave the icon out.
  • helpMarker shows (?).

Guard your own icon labels with iconsAvailable().

Text (CoreWidgets.h)#

  • heading(t, level), sectionTitle(t), overline(T)
  • textDim(fmt, ...), textFaint(fmt, ...), textColoured(c, fmt, ...), textMono(fmt, ...)
  • kbd("Ctrl+S"), helpMarker(t), tooltip(t)
  • clippedText(list, pos, w, c, t), centredText(list, min, max, c, t)

Buttons#

  • toneColour(Tone): the palette colour of a tone (neutral is textDim).
  • button(label, Variant, size). The variants are secondary, primary, ghost, outline, danger and success.
  • Shortcuts: primaryButton, dangerButton, ghostButton.
  • iconTextButton(icon, label, variant)
  • iconButton(icon, tooltip, active, activeColour, size)
  • toggleButton(label, &b, onColour, size, tooltip): compact pills such as M, S and R.
  • toggleSwitch(label, &b)
  • segmented(id, labels, n, &current, width). A width of -1 fills the row.
  • linkText(label)

Values#

  • knob(id, &v, min, max, default, KnobStyle{diameter, colour, label, format, unit}). Set KnobStyle.flags to knobBipolar, knobLogarithmic, knobInteger or knobNoLabel. .steps and .modulation are also available.
  • fader(id, &dB, minDb, maxDb, size, colour)
  • meter(id, size, peakL, peakR, rmsL, rmsR, vertical)
  • dragValue(id, &v, speed, min, max, fmt, width). speed is per pixel dragged. Once the field has the focus (clicked or navigated to), a wheel notch moves 10 × speed; before that, the wheel scrolls the panel. min >= max is unbounded.
  • sliderBar(id, &v, min, max, fmt, width, colour). A click or a drag sets the value. A wheel notch moves 1 % of the range.
  • valueEntry(...): the typed number field these controls open. valueEntryOpen() says whether one is open (to hold back shortcuts while the user types).
  • itemWheel(): the wheel for your own control, claimed in time so the panel under it does not scroll. Also takeWheel(), wheelTaken() and valueSpeed().

The value controls share these interactions:

  • drag to change; Ctrl is fine (× 0.15), Shift is fast (× 4)
  • the mouse wheel nudges the value and does not scroll the panel under it (a dragValue only once it has the focus)
  • a double click types the value (dragValue, sliderBar) or resets it (a knob)
  • a click on a knob's value types it

Fields#

  • searchField(id, buf, size, hint, width)
  • textField(id, buf, size, hint, width)
  • combo(id, &i, items, n, width)

Quick filtering (Filter.h, included in Core)#

Provide a quick filter in menus and panels where users need to find actions or properties. Keep a TextFilter in each view's state. filterBox(id, state) draws the query field; panelHeader(title, subtitle, &state) includes it in the heading. Use state.matches(englishLabel, keywordsAndSectionPath) before drawing a row. Search uses all words, ignoring ASCII/Latin case and accents, and checks both the English key and the current translation. Hidden ImGui IDs are excluded.

beginFilteredSection(label, state, hasMatchingChildren, defaultOpen) reveals a matching section without changing its saved collapse preference; pair with endSection() when true. filterMenu(id, state, entries) draws a searchable menu inside an already open ImGui menu/popup. Its FilterMenuItem tree retains action IDs, disabled/checked states and shortcuts. Searching lists matching descendants with breadcrumbs. The host handles the returned action ID.

InspectorOptions{&state, sectionTitle} enables filtering in inspector(); propertyMatches(state, property, sectionTitle) helps choose visible sections. Call Inspector for a section's full property model so hidden active edits can be cancelled; when omitting an entire panel, cancel its host previews explicitly. Read FILTERING.md for complete C++ and Python examples and limits. These helpers do not intercept raw ImGui calls or patch Dear ImGui.

Containers#

  • beginCard(id, title, height, tone) / endCard(). Always call endCard, whatever beginCard returned.
  • beginSection(label, defaultOpen) / endSection(). Call endSection only when beginSection returned true.
  • beginProperties(id, labelWidth) / property(label, help) / endProperties(). Call endProperties only when beginProperties returned true. property() sets up full width for the next widget.
  • toolbarSeparator(), divider(spacing), space(h)

Status#

  • badge(t, Tone), statusDot(c, tip)
  • progressBar(f, size, overlay, Tone). A fraction f < 0 gives an indeterminate bar.
  • spinner(id, r, c)
  • emptyState(title, msg, icon)
  • callout(Tone, text)
  • colourChip(id, c, size)
  • notify(text, Tone, seconds) shows a toast in the current ImGui context. With no context current, it goes to the one context CyUI knows. When there are several or none, it asserts in debug builds and drops the toast. notify(context, text, Tone, seconds) posts to a given context, from any thread. Call renderNotifications() once per frame. At most six toasts show at a time.

Layout (Layout.h)#

The application shell. Call these in the frame in this order: menu bar, top bar, status bar, sidebar, then dock space.

  • beginTopBar(id, h) / endTopBar()
  • beginStatusBar(id) / endStatusBar(), with statusText(Tone, fmt, ...)
  • beginSidebar(id, w) / endSidebar(), with sidebarHeader(title, badge), sidebarGroup(LABEL) and sidebarItem(icon, label, active, badge)
  • dockSpace(id, flags) (docking branch)
  • panelHeader(title, subtitle)
  • panelHeader(title, subtitle, &filter) to add a quick filter
  • beginToolbar(id) / endToolbar()
  • beginModal(title, &open, width) / endModal(). Call endModal only when beginModal returned true. modalButtons(confirm, cancel, danger) returns 1 for confirm and 2 for cancel. Enter confirms and Escape cancels. Modals can nest: each modalButtons closes its own modal.
  • alignRight(width), buttonWidth(label)

All begin*Bar / beginSidebar / beginToolbar must be paired with their end*, whatever they returned. Popups and tooltips opened from a bar keep the theme's style.

Gallery (Gallery.h)#

  • showGallery(&open, selectTab): every widget, a theme switcher and a density switcher. selectTab brings a page to the front once:
    • 0 text, 1 buttons, 2 controls, 3 containers
    • 4–19 the optional modules
    • 20 layout (the application shell), 21 filtering (menus and panels)
  • showGallery(&open, selectTab, GalleryResources): the same, with host resources for the module pages: texture, width and height (Images, Viewport), web (a live Web backend) and previewCommands.
  • showThemeEditor(&open): live palette editing and .cytheme save and load.

GalleryResources::openDocumentation(page, section) optionally routes the Filtering example’s Help action to the host’s local reader at filtering/searchable-menus. Keep its callback owner alive during drawing. Gallery does not launch a browser itself.
